scenarios.desc: Ephemeris & ground track — "where is the satellite right now".
scenarios.kindDesc: Ephemeris & ground track: propagate one satellite (TLE→SGP4 or analytic orbit) and emit its TEME/GCRS state (position + velocity), ITRF/ECEF position, WGS-84 sub-satellite lat/lon/alt, and per-step station az/el/range + range-rate (Doppler). The satellite comes from a `tle` or from an analytic `orbit` with its `epoch` (a `tle` wins when both are given); with a `tle`, an `epoch` overrides the TLE's own epoch as t = 0.
scenarios.toml:
kind = "ephemeris"

# Ephemeris & ground track — "where is the satellite right now".
#
# Propagate the ISS (ZARYA) for one revolution and emit, at every 30 s step: the
# inertial TEME and GCRS (≈ J2000) state (position AND velocity), the Earth-fixed
# ITRF/ECEF position, the WGS-84 sub-satellite point (latitude / longitude /
# altitude — the ground track drawn in the chart), and the topocentric azimuth /
# elevation / range and range-rate (the geometric Doppler) seen from a ground
# station. The frame chain is the one validated to the millimetre against the
# published Vallado vectors; the velocity is validated against the official AIAA
# tcppver vectors.
#
# A TLE's epoch is its own (UTC); the ground track therefore starts at the TLE
# epoch. Swap in any current TLE (e.g. from CelesTrak) to track a live satellite.
tle = """
1 25544U 98067A   20045.18587073  .00000950  00000-0  25302-4 0  9990
2 25544  51.6443 242.0161 0004885 264.6060 207.3845 15.49165514212791
"""
step_s = 30.0
duration_s = 16740.0   # ~three ISS revolutions

# Earth-orientation: dut1_s = UT1 - UTC (0 => the DUT1 ~ 0 approximation, a few-
# arcsecond / few-hundred-metre longitude shift in the ground track); xp_arcsec /
# yp_arcsec are the IERS polar-motion pole coordinates. Leave at 0 for a quick run,
# or supply IERS values.
dut1_s = 0.0
xp_arcsec = 0.0
yp_arcsec = 0.0

# Optional ground station — ESA's European Space Operations Centre, Darmstadt.
# Drives the az / el / range and the range-rate / Doppler columns.
[station]
lat_deg = 49.8707
lon_deg = 8.6217
alt_m = 144.0

scenarios.desc: Positioning a lander on Europa: the Jovian-moon case.
scenarios.kindDesc: Positioning around any solar-system body: an orbiter or a surface lander around a central body chosen by name (Mars, the Moon, Europa, Ganymede, Titan and the rest of the solar-system catalogue), navigating with one-way pseudoranges from a small Walker navigation constellation around the body (two-body orbits with the body's own J2 secular drift, an unknown user clock) and optionally a clock-free deep-space two-way range from the Earth, whose direction and distance come from the analytic solar-system ephemeris at every epoch. Lines of sight are blocked by the body's mean sphere, and a surface user also needs the elevation mask. Per epoch: relays in view, whether the Earth is above the limb, the constellation-only GDOP and PDOP (geometric and position dilution of precision), the formal one-sigma position uncertainty with and without the Earth row, and the error of a seeded Gauss-Newton least-squares fix each way; over the run: availability, Earth visibility, median PDOP, RMS error and median formal sigma, plus the Earth-to-body light time, round trip, Shapiro delay and Sun separation at the epoch. MODELLED: the relay orbits, the noise levels and the instantaneous measurement model are modelling choices, not validated against a mission's navigation data; the body constants are the published values cited in body.rs, and the Earth geometry inherits the solar-system ephemeris labels.
scenarios.toml:
# Positioning a lander on Europa: the Jovian-moon case.
#
# A lander at 20 deg north, 60 deg east on Europa's surface navigates for one Europan day
# (3.55 Earth days, the synchronous rotation period) with twelve navigation satellites at
# 4 500 km in three planes inclined 55 deg, under a 10 deg elevation mask, and a two-way
# range from Earth whenever the Earth is above the lander's horizon. Europa is tidally
# locked, so from a fixed site Jupiter never moves in the sky, while the Earth, riding
# with Jupiter, rises and sets once per Europan day: the Earth link is available only for
# part of the run, and the report shows what the local constellation must carry alone.
#
# The Europa constants (gravitational parameter, mean radius, International Astronomical
# Union (IAU) pole and prime meridian)
# are the published values cited in src/body.rs; no J2 (second zonal harmonic) is carried
# for Europa, so the relay
# orbits are two-body. The Earth-Europa light time is about 36 minutes one way at this
# epoch, near a Jupiter opposition.
#
# One simplification matters more here than at Mars: the relays orbit inside Europa's Hill
# sphere (about 13 700 km) but Jupiter's pull on them is not modelled, so their orbits are
# idealised. The run shows the geometry and what the Earth link adds (availability rises
# from about half the Europan day to about three quarters), not a flyable design.
#
# MODELLED: the constellation, the noise and the measurement model are modelling choices.
kind = "body-pnt"
body = "Europa"
epoch = "2027-02-19T00:00:00"
duration_s = 306822.0
step_s = 1800.0
seed = 11

[user]
kind = "surface"
lat_deg = 20.0
lon_deg = 60.0

[constellation]
planes = 3
sats_per_plane = 4
altitude_km = 4500.0
inclination_deg = 55.0
sigma_range_m = 1.0
mask_deg = 10.0

[earth_link]
enabled = true
sigma_range_m = 1.0

scenarios.desc: Joint sensor-fusion PNT: a single Kalman filter is the navigator, fusing the clock and inertial states and aided by optical ISL time transfer, rather than composing independent predictors. GNSS denied 1.8 h.
scenarios.kindDesc: Joint Kalman sensor-fusion PNT over the same hybrid inputs.
scenarios.toml:
# Joint sensor-fusion PNT: a single Kalman filter is the navigator, fusing the
# clock and inertial states and aided by optical ISL time transfer, rather than
# composing independent predictors. GNSS denied 1.8 h.
#
# The filter learns the clock frequency offset and the platform velocity while
# GNSS is available, then coasts through the outage propagating those estimates;
# its joint covariance gives the joint integrity. To keep the filter's process
# noise consistent with truth, the accelerometers here are noise-driven (bias set
# to zero) — augmented-state estimation of constant biases is future work.
# Vendor-neutral; clock and noise parameters are public/cited or illustrative.
kind = "fusion"
seed = 42
timing_spec_ns = 20.0
position_spec_m = 100.0

[time]
step_s = 10.0
duration_s = 7200.0

[gnss]
windows = [
  { t0 = 0.0,   t1 = 600.0,  state = "nominal" },
  { t0 = 600.0, t1 = 7200.0, state = "denied" },
]

[resync]
enabled = true
interval_s = 1800.0
sigma_j_s = 1.0e-12

[clock_quantum]
id = "optical-sr-lattice"
provenance = "Strontium optical lattice clock, space-oriented goal sigma_y(1s)=1e-15 (arXiv:1503.08457)"
y0 = 5.0e-17
q_wf = 1.0e-30
q_rw = 0.0
drift = 0.0

[clock_classical]
id = "csac-sa45s"
provenance = "Microchip SA65 / SA.45s CSAC datasheet sigma_y(1s)=3e-10"
y0 = 5.0e-10
q_wf = 9.0e-20
q_rw = 0.0
drift = 0.0

[accel_quantum]
id = "cold-atom-quat"
provenance = "Cold-atom accelerometer, low long-tau velocity-random-walk; illustrative noise-driven value (bias zeroed for filter consistency)"
bias = 0.0
q_va = 1.0e-9

[accel_classical]
id = "nav-grade-quartz"
provenance = "Navigation-grade quartz accelerometer; illustrative noise-driven value (bias zeroed for filter consistency)"
bias = 0.0
q_va = 1.0e-7

scenarios.desc: Loosely-coupled GNSS/INS: the three-axis strapdown navigator disciplined by a 15-state error-state EKF, then coasting through a 60 s GNSS outage. Unlike the `inertial` pack (a 1-DOF scalar dead-reckoner with a truth-snap reset at every fix), this runs the genuine closed-loop filter: it learns from noisy fixes while GNSS is up and coasts on the corrected state during the gap. The reported error is the real horizontal residual against truth; each sensor also carries its open-loop free-INS RMS so the filter's value is explicit.
scenarios.kindDesc: Loosely- and tightly-coupled GNSS/INS error-state EKF.
scenarios.toml:
# Loosely-coupled GNSS/INS: the three-axis strapdown navigator disciplined by a
# 15-state error-state EKF, then coasting through a 60 s GNSS outage. Unlike the
# `inertial` pack (a 1-DOF scalar dead-reckoner with a truth-snap reset at every
# fix), this runs the genuine closed-loop filter: it learns from noisy fixes while
# GNSS is up and coasts on the corrected state during the gap. The reported error
# is the real horizontal residual against truth; each sensor also carries its
# open-loop free-INS RMS so the filter's value is explicit.
#
# Honest framing: loosely-coupled, a single deterministic driving trajectory, a
# flat-Earth tangent-plane INS<->GNSS comparison. The lower-bias (quantum-grade)
# sensor has the better unaided coast. Both biases here are constant and noise-free,
# so the filter learns them while GNSS is up and the fused coast is a best case; a
# bias that keeps drifting is what ends a real one (see small-uas-jammed-nav.toml).
# Revised in 0.27.3: a sign error in the filter's gyro-bias coupling had put a floor
# of tens of metres under the fused outage error; see the CHANGELOG.
kind = "gnss-ins"
seed = 7
threshold_m = 50.0
fix_interval_s = 1.0
sigma_pos_m = 1.0
sigma_vel_mps = 0.05
lat_deg = 45.0
lon_deg = -57.3
alt_m = 50.0

[time]
step_s = 0.1
duration_s = 160.0

[gnss]
windows = [
  { t0 = 0.0,   t1 = 100.0, state = "nominal" },
  { t0 = 100.0, t1 = 160.0, state = "denied" },
]

[imu_quantum]
id = "cold-atom-imu"
provenance = "Quantum-grade inertial unit: low residual accelerometer/gyro bias (cold-atom-class); the better unaided coast"
accel_bias = [0.015, 0.0, 0.0]
gyro_bias = [0.0, 0.0, 5.0e-5]

[imu_classical]
id = "tactical-imu"
provenance = "Tactical-grade MEMS/quartz inertial unit: larger residual bias; the free-running INS diverges much faster"
accel_bias = [0.03, -0.02, 0.0]
gyro_bias = [0.0, 0.0, 1.0e-4]

# Optional: layer the full deterministic IMU error chain on top of the constant
# biases above. Every field defaults to zero, so omitting this block leaves the
# sensor a pure constant-bias source (the run is then identical to before this
# schema existed). The terms drive the three-axis strapdown mechanization through
# the IMU error model (IEEE Std 952-1997 §A.2; Groves 2013 §4.3). Scale-factor is
# in ppm; misalignment in rad (off-diagonal); g-sensitivity in (rad/s)/(m/s²);
# quantization in the sensor's output units; rate-ramp is a linear-in-time drift.
# [imu_classical.error_model]
# scale_gyro_ppm  = [1500.0, 1500.0, 1500.0]
# scale_accel_ppm = [1000.0, 1000.0, 1000.0]
# g_sensitivity   = [5.0e-5, 5.0e-5, 5.0e-5]
# rate_ramp_gyro  = [0.0, 1.0e-6, 0.0]
# quant_gyro      = [1.0e-5, 1.0e-5, 1.0e-5]

scenarios.desc: Measurement-domain GNSS simulation: pseudoranges with ionospheric and tropospheric delays, fed to snapshot RAIM for protection levels.
scenarios.kindDesc: Measurement-domain pseudorange simulation (Klobuchar iono, Saastamoinen/Niell tropo) + RAIM.
scenarios.toml:
# Measurement-domain GNSS simulation: pseudoranges with ionospheric and
# tropospheric delays, fed to snapshot RAIM for protection levels.
#
# Unlike the purely-geometric `orbit` pack (visibility + DOP only), this synthesises
# each visible satellite's pseudorange:
#   ρ = geometric range + c·δt_rx − c·δt_sv + I(Klobuchar) + T(Saastamoinen·Niell)
#       + thermal noise + multipath
# and forms the measurement residuals that drive snapshot RAIM (HPL/VPL, fault
# detection). The per-epoch per-satellite measurements are emitted in the JSON
# `gnss_measurements` array for downstream tools.
kind = "gnss-sim"
seed = 7
mask_deg = 5.0
noise_sigma_m = 1.5      # 1σ thermal noise per pseudorange (set 0 for a noise-free run)
multipath_m = 0.5        # peak deterministic multipath, scaled by (1 − sin elevation)
sat_clock_rms_m = 30.0   # peak per-PRN satellite clock offset
uere_m = 3.0             # RAIM 1σ user-equivalent range error
p_fa = 1.0e-5
p_md = 1.0e-3
alert_limit_h_m = 40.0
alert_limit_v_m = 50.0

[time]
step_s = 60.0
duration_s = 3600.0

[receiver]
lat_deg = 40.4
lon_deg = -3.7
alt_m = 660.0
clock_bias_m = 1500.0

# A GPS-like 24-satellite Walker shell propagated through the validated SGP4 core.
[constellation]
altitude_km = 20200.0
inclination_deg = 55.0
planes = 6
sats_per_plane = 4
phasing_f = 1.0

# Klobuchar single-frequency ionosphere (IS-GPS-200 §20.3.3.5.2.5): the eight
# broadcast coefficients and the GPS seconds-of-day at the start of the run.
[iono]
alpha = [3.82e-8, 1.49e-8, -1.79e-7, 0.0]
beta = [1.43e5, 0.0, -3.28e5, 1.13e5]
gps_seconds_of_day = 50400.0

# Saastamoinen zenith troposphere (Davis 1985 / Groves §9.4) with Niell (1996)
# mapping: surface meteorology and the day-of-year.
[tropo]
pressure_hpa = 1013.25
temp_k = 288.15
humidity = 0.5
day_of_year = 180.0

scenarios.desc: 60-minute GPS-denied gravity-map-matching benchmark (quantum alt-PNT).
scenarios.kindDesc: GPS-denied gravity-map-matching navigation: a cold-atom gravimeter recovers a constant INS drift from the gravity-anomaly sequence it flies through.
scenarios.toml:
# 60-minute GPS-denied gravity-map-matching benchmark (quantum alt-PNT).
#
# The validation-grade form of `gravity-map-nav.toml`: a vehicle flies a ~700 km track for
# a full one-hour GNSS outage, its inertial solution drifting to ≈ 70 km of position error.
# A cold-atom gravimeter samples the gravity anomaly along the track (with its real, seeded
# white-noise floor injected), and a hierarchical coarse-to-fine particle/grid matcher
# recovers the constant INS drift to a few hundred metres — the < 500 m GPS-denied target
# of ESA NAVISP's "Quantum Wayfarer" gravity-aided navigation.
#
# Consumed by `kshana::gravimeter::run_gps_denied_gravity_nav` (and its unit tests). The
# reference field is a low-degree spherical-harmonic trend plus synthetic mascons; Kshana
# does not bundle the full EGM2008 coefficient set, and a Monte-Carlo over map-representation
# error realisations is a documented follow-on (see docs/CAPABILITY.md).

# Dispatched by the scenario engine as `kind = "gravity-map"` (also consumed directly by
# `run_gps_denied_gravity_nav` in the unit tests, which ignore this field).
kind = "gravity-map"

# Maximum spherical-harmonic degree/order of the reference field.
nmax = 3

# Track flown GPS-denied: 90 waypoints, 40 s gravimeter averaging each ⇒ 3600 s = 60 min.
# An oblique leg keeps the scalar gravimeter sequence observable in both north and east.
start_lat_deg = 10.0
start_lon_deg = 20.0
step_lat_deg = 0.06
step_lon_deg = 0.045
waypoints = 90

# True constant INS position drift accumulated over the one-hour outage (≈ 70 km at ~13° lat,
# i.e. far past the 10 km the matched solution must beat).
drift_lat_deg = 0.5
drift_lon_deg = -0.4

# Cold-atom gravimeter: 1e-7 m/s²/√Hz ASD (≈10 µGal/√Hz), 40 s averaging ⇒ σ ≈ 1.6e-3 mGal.
gravimeter_asd = 1.0e-7
averaging_time_s = 40.0

# Map/representation error (mGal): combined with the sensor white noise into the matching σ.
map_sigma_mgal = 2.0

# Hierarchical offset search: ±0.8° at 0.08° to start, then three coarse-to-fine stages each
# shrinking the window and step 8× ⇒ final offset resolution 0.08° / 8² ≈ 140 m.
search_half_deg = 0.8
search_step_deg = 0.08
refine_stages = 3
refine_factor = 8.0
noise_seed = 1

# Low-degree anomalous, fully-normalised coefficients (the always-on regional trend).
[[coeffs]]
n = 2
m = 0
cbar = 6.0e-6
sbar = 0.0

[[coeffs]]
n = 3
m = 1
cbar = 3.0e-6
sbar = 2.0e-6

# Localized Gaussian anomalies (mascons) the track crosses — the distinctive high-degree
# features that make the constant drift observable.
[[mascons]]
lat_deg = 11.0
lon_deg = 20.8
amp_mgal = 45.0
sigma_deg = 0.30

[[mascons]]
lat_deg = 12.4
lon_deg = 21.9
amp_mgal = -38.0
sigma_deg = 0.28

[[mascons]]
lat_deg = 13.8
lon_deg = 23.0
amp_mgal = 50.0
sigma_deg = 0.32

scenarios.desc: Quantum gravity-map-matching navigation scenario (GPS-denied alt-PNT).
scenarios.kindDesc: GPS-denied gravity-map-matching navigation: a cold-atom gravimeter recovers a constant INS drift from the gravity-anomaly sequence it flies through.
scenarios.toml:
# Quantum gravity-map-matching navigation scenario (GPS-denied alt-PNT).
#
# Targets ESA NAVISP "Quantum Wayfarer" / QT-CCI gravity-map-matching vocabulary: a
# vehicle with an inertial unit and a cold-atom-interferometer gravimeter navigates with
# no GNSS by matching the gravity-anomaly signature it flies through against a stored
# reference field. The reference field is a low-degree spherical-harmonic anomaly plus
# synthetic mascons — Kshana does not bundle the full EGM2008 coefficient set (see
# docs/CAPABILITY.md).
#
# This is a runnable scenario kind: the CLI dispatches `kind = "gravity-map"` to
# `kshana::gravimeter::run_gps_denied_gravity_nav` (the validation-grade noisy/refined
# form) and emits JSON + an SVG drift chart (free-inertial vs gravity-matched error).
# The same config also backs `run_gravity_map_benchmark` (the noise-free geometric-
# observability benchmark) and its unit test, which read this file directly.
kind = "gravity-map"

# Maximum spherical-harmonic degree/order of the reference field.
nmax = 3

# Track flown GPS-denied: an oblique leg so the scalar gravimeter sequence is observable
# in both north and east (a single anomaly measurement only constrains a level set).
start_lat_deg = 12.0
start_lon_deg = 24.0
step_lat_deg = 0.18
step_lon_deg = 0.13
waypoints = 12

# True constant INS position drift accumulated over the outage (≈ 80 km at ~13° lat).
drift_lat_deg = 0.55
drift_lon_deg = -0.45

# Cold-atom gravimeter: 1e-7 m/s²/√Hz ASD (≈10 µGal/√Hz), 100 s averaging ⇒ σ ≈ 1e-3 mGal.
gravimeter_asd = 1.0e-7
averaging_time_s = 100.0

# Map/representation error (mGal): reference-field inaccuracy + grid quantisation, combined
# with the sensor white noise into the effective matching σ. Dominates a quantum gravimeter.
map_sigma_mgal = 2.0

# Offset search grid (degrees): ±1.0° at 0.05° resolution around the no-drift prior.
search_half_deg = 1.0
search_step_deg = 0.05

# Low-degree anomalous, fully-normalised coefficients (the regional trend).
[[coeffs]]
n = 2
m = 0
cbar = 4.0e-6
sbar = 0.0

[[coeffs]]
n = 3
m = 1
cbar = 2.0e-6
sbar = 1.0e-6

# Localized Gaussian anomalies (mascons) the track crosses — the stand-in for the
# high-degree EGM features that make gravity-map matching observable.
[[mascons]]
lat_deg = 13.0
lon_deg = 25.0
amp_mgal = 32.0
sigma_deg = 0.45

[[mascons]]
lat_deg = 12.6
lon_deg = 24.6
amp_mgal = -26.0
sigma_deg = 0.35

scenarios.desc: Heterogeneous optical + RF PNT joint availability / precision / integrity (P5).
scenarios.kindDesc: MODELLED heterogeneous optical + RF PNT joint figure of merit (P5): composes the 1550 nm two-way optical link budget (photon-limited two-way ranging CRLB σ_τ/√N and diffraction footprint λ/D·range), a cross-modality solution-separation RAIM protection level (position AND timing) that fuses the loose RF and tight optical solutions with disparate covariances, the N-station optical clear-sky availability (independent-union 1−Π(1−a_i) and a spatially-correlated variant), an optical↔RF state/covariance handoff with a PROVEN bit-continuous (no-jump) mean and a NEES χ² consistency gate, and a joint P(available AND precision-grade AND integrity-assured) score with correlation handling. VALIDATED closed form: the ranging CRLB, diffraction footprint, χ² protection-level quantile, union combinatorics, handoff mean-continuity + NEES gate, and the joint independent product. MODELLED: the optical loss allocations, RF/optical σ magnitudes, cloud-climatology inputs, correlations, and P_HMI budget. Not a certified availability/integrity product.
scenarios.toml:
# Heterogeneous optical + RF PNT joint availability / precision / integrity (P5).
#
# Composes the Phase-7 pieces into one end-to-end analysis:
#   * L26 optical link budget  -> photon-limited two-way ranging CRLB + diffraction footprint
#   * L22 cross-modality RAIM   -> position AND timing protection level (loose RF x tight optical)
#   * L24 optical availability  -> N-station clear-sky diversity (independent + correlated union)
#   * L23 optical<->RF handoff  -> proven bit-continuous (no-jump) mean + NEES chi-square gate
#   * L25 joint FoM             -> P(available AND precision-grade AND integrity-assured)
#
# MODELLED. Validated closed forms: ranging CRLB (sigma_tau/sqrt(N)), diffraction footprint
# (lambda/D * range), chi-square protection-level quantile, union combinatorics, handoff
# mean-continuity + NEES gate, and the joint independent product. The loss allocations,
# sigma magnitudes, cloud-climatology inputs, correlations and P_HMI budget are Modelled
# representative inputs. Every field below is optional and shown at its default.
kind = "hybrid-optical-rf"

# --- L26 optical (1550 nm) two-way link budget ---
wavelength_nm      = 1550.0     # telecom C-band, eye-safe, low atmospheric loss
tx_power_w         = 1.0e-3     # 1 mW mean optical power (photon-starved lunar regime)
tx_aperture_m      = 0.85       # -> ~0.7 km diffraction footprint at lunar range (lambda/D)
rx_aperture_m      = 0.85
range_km           = 384000.0   # mean Earth-Moon distance
pulse_rms_ps       = 50.0       # signal-pulse RMS temporal width
integration_s      = 1.0
atmospheric_loss_db = 3.0       # Modelled 1550 nm clear-sky allocation
pointing_loss_db    = 3.0       # Modelled terminal pointing/jitter allocation
optics_efficiency   = 0.5       # Modelled
detector_efficiency = 0.7       # Modelled
two_way             = true      # round-trip ranging: range = c*dt/2, double-pass geometry

# --- RF (loose) reference solution ---
rf_pos_sigma_m      = 1.0       # horizontal 1-sigma
rf_vertical_sigma_m = 1.5       # vertical 1-sigma (vertical dilution)
rf_clock_sigma_s    = 3.0e-9    # 3 ns clock 1-sigma

# --- L22 cross-modality RAIM ---
p_fa              = 1.0e-5
p_md              = 1.0e-3
alert_limit_h_m   = 10.0
alert_limit_v_m   = 15.0
alert_limit_t_s   = 20.0e-9

# --- precision grade (the high-grade service the FoM scores) ---
grade_pos_m  = 0.1              # 10 cm position grade
grade_time_s = 1.0e-9           # 1 ns timing grade

# --- L24 optical ground-network availability ---
n_optical_sites  = 5
site_correlation = 0.15         # representative modest spatial (weather) correlation

# --- L25 joint FoM + L23 handoff ---
fom_correlation   = 0.5         # positive co-occurrence of the three P5 conditions
handoff_inflation = 0.2         # modality-transition covariance inflation at the switch
p_hmi             = 1.0e-7      # integrity-risk budget

# --- G15 bias / ramp fault injection against the cross-modality monitor ---
# The minimum detectable bias and the detection-power curve are ANALYTIC (non-central
# chi-square inversion), so they need no inputs of their own. These two only set the ramp
# rate the reported time-to-detect is a rate conversion of. Both MODELLED.
fault_ramp_rate_pos_m_s   = 0.05      # position-axis bias growth (m/s)
fault_ramp_rate_clock_s_s = 1.0e-11   # clock-axis bias growth (s/s)

# --- G17 post-handover coast: process noise and the alert-limit crossing ---
# Random walk on the existing 4-state (east, north, up, clock) handoff filter. The alert
# limits are the ones already declared above; only the process noise and the coverage
# factor are new. Both PSDs are MODELLED representative inputs and the crossing times
# scale directly with them.
process_noise_pos_psd_m2_s   = 1.0e-3   # 1 m (1-sigma) of unmodelled growth per 1000 s, per axis
process_noise_clock_psd_s2_s = 1.0e-22  # white-FM phase random walk at sigma_y(1 s) = 1e-11
# coast_coverage_k                      # default Phi^-1(1 - P_HMI/2) = 5.327; uncomment to override

# --- G16 RF link leg: availability, and the like-for-like ranging comparison ---
# The RF side of a hybrid service needs its own link, and this is it. Both the RF
# availability block (A_rf = I_closure * I_track over the Eb/N0 margin and the tracking
# threshold) and the RF leg of the optical-versus-RF ranging ratio are evaluated from
# exactly these values, at the range_km and integration_s already declared above, so the
# two modalities can never be compared at different operating points.
rf_band                     = "x"       # s | x | ka -> the CCSDS-401 / DSN-810-005 band centre
rf_eirp_dbw                 = 26.0      # MODELLED: the lunar augmented-forward-signal EIRP
rf_g_over_t_db              = 53.0      # MODELLED: DSN 34 m beam-waveguide X-band figure of merit
rf_other_losses_db          = 3.0       # MODELLED: lumped pointing/polarisation/atmosphere/implementation
rf_data_rate_bps            = 1.0e6     # sets Eb/N0 and the closure margin; does not touch C/N0
rf_required_eb_n0_db        = 4.5
rf_chip_rate_hz             = 1.023e6   # GPS C/A reference chip rate
rf_correlator_spacing_chips = 0.5       # standard half-chip early-late correlator
rf_tracking_threshold_dbhz  = 25.0      # MODELLED receiver loss-of-lock threshold
rf_degraded_margin_db       = 6.0       # MODELLED: DEGRADED band above that threshold
# rf_dll_bandwidth_hz                   # DERIVED as 1/(2*integration_s) = 0.5 Hz, the loop
#                                       # noise bandwidth whose equivalent averaging time is
#                                       # exactly the optical accumulation time. Overriding it
#                                       # so the two disagree REFUSES the ranging ratio rather
#                                       # than quoting one at two operating points.

scenarios.desc: Hybrid PNT capstone: all-quantum suite (optical clock + cold-atom IMU + optical ISL time-transfer aiding) vs all-classical suite (CSAC + nav-grade IMU + RF). GNSS denied 1.8 h.

scenarios.desc: 17-state hybrid quantum + classical tightly-coupled GNSS/INS UKF (MODELLED).
scenarios.kindDesc: 17-state hybrid quantum+classical tightly-coupled GNSS/INS UKF (MODELLED): 15 INS error states + CAI-derived accel-bias correction + a 2-state (phase+frequency) clock from the q-parameter clock engine, driven by the bracketed CAI error model. The figure of merit is filter self-consistency (NEES + innovation-whiteness vs χ² bounds) — a self-consistency statement, NOT a real-world accuracy guarantee. Simulation only; no TRL>3, no flight heritage, no external validation.
scenarios.toml:
# 17-state hybrid quantum + classical tightly-coupled GNSS/INS UKF (MODELLED).
#
# Surfaces the 17-state error-state unscented Kalman filter (src/fusion/tightly_coupled17.rs)
# as a runnable scenario. The state is:
#
#   x = [ p(3) | v(3) | psi(3) | b_a(3) | b_g(3) | b  d ]
#        position velocity attitude  accel-bias gyro-bias  clock(phase,freq)
#
#   * 15 INS error states (position, velocity, attitude misalignment, accel + gyro bias)
#     propagated through the strapdown mechanization driven by the IMU — the CLASSICAL
#     short-term inertial solution.
#   * the accel-bias triad b_a is the CAI-DERIVED inertial bias correction: the cold-atom
#     interferometer below sets the velocity-random-walk floor q_va, so the long-term coast
#     drift is the QUANTUM-sensor-limited one — the quantum long-term half of the hybrid.
#   * the two-state clock [b, d] (phase + frequency, in range units) is driven by the
#     q-parameter clock engine (clock_state::q_from_allan) from the Allan profile below.
#
# The platform is GNSS-aided for a 100 s lead-in (the filter learns the biases, velocity and
# clock), then coasts through a 120 s GNSS outage on the CAI IMU + clock alone.
#
# FIGURE OF MERIT — filter self-consistency (NEES + innovation-whiteness), the only thing a
# simulation can honestly assert about an estimator. Over a Monte-Carlo ensemble whose truth
# is generated from exactly the noise the filter assumes, the pooled NIS (whiteness) and NEES
# means must land inside their 95% chi-squared bands. This is a SELF-CONSISTENCY statement,
# NOT a real-world accuracy guarantee.
#
# HONESTY: everything here is MODELLED / SIMULATION. The CAI and clock inputs are bracketed,
# literature-representative values, not measured hardware; the CAI hardware and its Key-Person
# stay partner-owned. No TRL>3, no flight heritage, no external validation.
kind = "hybrid-ukf"
seed = 1771

# Residual accelerometer bias the CAI-derived correction state estimates (m/s^2), body x-axis.
# A cold-atom-grade post-calibration residual (illustrative, bracketed).
residual_accel_bias_m_s2 = 1.0e-4

# Constant-velocity surface trajectory (+y, m/s).
speed_m_s = 100.0

# GNSS measurement noise (1-sigma): ~1 m code pseudorange, ~5 cm/s Doppler (Groves 2013 §9.3).
sigma_pr_m = 1.0
sigma_rr_mps = 0.05

# Monte-Carlo seeds the consistency oracle pools over, and the filter mistuning multipliers.
# 24 seeds give run-based chi-squared NEES bands (8*24 DOF) tight enough to discriminate a
# matched from a mistuned filter while keeping the run cheap. Set q_factor / r_factor away
# from 1.0 to mistune the filter and watch the consistency gate reject it (q_factor scales the
# assumed process noise, r_factor the assumed measurement noise).
consistency_seeds = 24
q_factor = 1.0
r_factor = 1.0

[time]
step_s = 0.5
duration_s = 220.0

[gnss]
windows = [
  { t0 = 0.0,   t1 = 100.0, state = "nominal" },
  { t0 = 100.0, t1 = 220.0, state = "denied" },
]

# Inertial sensor. The [accel.cai] block makes this the QUANTUM cold-atom interferometer: its
# velocity-random-walk floor q_va is derived from the interferometer physics (k_eff = 4*pi/lambda,
# projection noise 1/(C*sqrt(N)), cycle time), NOT from the supplied q_va. Remove the [accel.cai]
# block to fall back to a classical datasheet sensor at the supplied q_va.
[accel]
id = "cold-atom-interferometer"
provenance = "Cold-atom (Rb-87 D2) interferometric accelerometer; bracketed parameters in the GAIN/MAIUS literature range (Freier et al. arXiv:1512.05660; Becker et al. Nature 2018). Modelled, partner-owned hardware."
bias = 0.0
q_va = 1.0e-9          # fallback classical value (overridden by the [accel.cai] physics below)

[accel.cai]
wavelength_m = 780.241209e-9   # Rb-87 D2 line (RB87_D2_WAVELENGTH_M)
pulse_sep_t = 0.02              # interrogation pulse separation T (s)
atom_number = 1.0e6            # detected atoms per shot N
contrast = 0.5                # initial fringe contrast C0
cycle_time_s = 0.5            # measurement cycle time T_c (s)

# Onboard clock Allan profile, fed to the q-parameter clock engine. A space-oriented optical /
# ultra-stable oscillator class: white-FM sigma_y(1 s) ~ 1e-13, random-walk-FM two decades below.
[clock]
id = "ultrastable-optical"
provenance = "Ultra-stable/optical onboard oscillator class, white-FM sigma_y(1 s) ~ 1e-13 (Riley NIST SP 1065; bracketing the achievable, not a flight unit). Modelled."
white_fm_adev_1s = 1.0e-13
rw_fm_level = 1.0e-15

scenarios.desc: INS/TRN coasting error model — position error against coast duration, and the coast durations at which it crosses 10 m and 50 m.
scenarios.kindDesc: INS/TRN coasting error model: position error against coast duration, built from IMU coefficients rather than swept as an assumed drift rate. Five growth contributions, each with its own power of time — accelerometer bias (t²), gyro-bias tilt through gravity (t³), velocity random walk (t^1.5), angle random walk (t^2.5) and scale factor against travelled distance (t¹ cruising, t² under sustained specific force) — combined under a STATED rule (root-sum-square by default, or linear-sum, or deterministic-sum with stochastic-rss; all three are computed on every run so the choice is visible rather than buried). The coast durations reaching caller-supplied position thresholds (10 m and 50 m by default) are located by the engine's existing bisection, each with a per-contribution breakdown naming the dominant source, and each single contribution's crossing is additionally inverted algebraically so the two agree. A terrain-relative-navigation mode bounds the coast with periodic position fixes and reports the largest fix interval that holds each threshold; a position-only fix leaves velocity error and tilt alive across the fix, so it does not always bound the coast at any fix rate, and the report says so rather than returning a zero. MODELLED: the IMU class coefficients are representative band figures, not a datasheet, and the terrain-fix residual is an input. An unreached threshold is reported as null with a status, never as a zero. Not a certified inertial-navigation performance product.
scenarios.toml:
# INS/TRN coasting error model — position error against coast duration, and the coast
# durations at which it crosses 10 m and 50 m.
#
# The question this answers: when a GNSS (or aperture-duty-cycled) study says "assume a
# dead-reckoning drift of 0.001–0.050 m/s", where does that number come from? It comes
# from the IMU, and this scenario computes it instead of sweeping it. Five growth terms —
# accelerometer bias (t^2), gyro-bias tilt through gravity (t^3), velocity random walk
# (t^1.5), angle random walk (t^2.5) and scale factor times the travelled distance — are
# combined under a stated rule, and the threshold crossings are located by bisection on
# the combined model. Every crossing carries the per-contribution breakdown that says
# which error source put it there.
#
# Consumed by `kshana::inertial::coast` and dispatched as `kind = "ins-trn-coast"`. The
# growth laws are cross-checked against the engine's own stochastic dead-reckoner
# (`inertial::AccelModel`, Monte-Carlo) and its IMU error model
# (`inertial::imu_errors::ImuErrorModel`, double-integrated); the IMU class coefficients
# are representative Groves-Table-4.1-band figures, NOT a datasheet for any part.
kind = "ins-trn-coast"

# Representative IMU class: navigation, tactical, industrial or consumer. Any individual
# coefficient below can be overridden, which relabels the reported grade as `custom`.
imu_grade = "navigation"

# Airborne cruise. The scale-factor error mis-scales the TRAVELLED DISTANCE, so the speed
# is part of the error model, not decoration: at 250 m/s a 100 ppm scale factor is a
# 0.025 m/s floor on the mean drift rate that no coast duration falls below.
speed_m_s = 250.0
ref_accel_m_s2 = 0.0

# How the five contributions combine into one number. A MODELLING CHOICE, stated: `rss`
# reads each coefficient as a 1-sigma spec, `linear-sum` is the coherent worst case, and
# `det-sum-stoch-rss` adds the systematic terms while root-sum-squaring the independently
# driven random walks. All three are reported in `combination_sensitivity` either way.
combination = "rss"

# The crossings to report (m). These are inputs: the 10 m / 50 m pair is the default, not
# a constant compiled into the model.
crossing_thresholds_m = [10.0, 50.0]

# The drift-rate band a duty-cycle study sweeps (m/s), checked against per grade.
drift_band_lo_m_per_s = 0.001
drift_band_hi_m_per_s = 0.050

# Terrain-referenced aiding. TRN in this engine (`altpnt::terrain`, `altpnt::sequential`)
# recovers a POSITION offset by matching measured ground elevation against a stored DEM,
# so it bounds the coast with a fix rather than slowing the growth between fixes.
# `position-only` is what a bare position fix does — velocity error and tilt keep
# integrating across it; `full-reset` re-zeroes the whole error state, as
# `AccelModel::reset` does for a GNSS re-alignment.
trn_fix_mode = "position-only"
trn_fix_interval_s = 120.0
# The matching sigma of the shipped terrain-nav configuration: hypot(altimeter 8 m,
# DEM 15 m). NOT the achieved batch-matcher residual on that scenario's track.
trn_fix_residual_m = 17.0
mission_duration_s = 1200.0

# GNSS integrity (RAIM) availability over a GPS-like constellation.

# At each epoch the visible satellites are propagated, the snapshot-RAIM
# horizontal/vertical protection levels are computed from the geometry and the
# user-equivalent range error, and availability is judged against the APV-I
# alert limits (HAL 40 m, VAL 50 m). The output is an HPL/VPL availability map:

#
# The ranging error here (1 m, 1-sigma) is representative of a modern
# dual-frequency, carrier-smoothed receiver — single-frequency RAIM (~5-6 m) does
# not meet the vertical APV-I limit on a single constellation, which is why
# vertical guidance uses SBAS / dual-frequency / ARAIM. The constellation is a
# synthetic 24-satellite Walker-delta pattern (6 planes of 4), illustrative of
# GPS geometry; swap in a `tle` block for a real one.
#
# The result also carries a vertical Stanford(-ESA) integrity diagram: at each
# protected epoch a seeded no-fault range-error draw is mapped through the
# geometry to an actual vertical error and classified against the VPL and the
# vertical alert limit (Available / System-Unavailable / Misleading / Hazardously
# Misleading). `seed` makes that error realization reproducible.

scenarios.desc: RF jamming: a ground-based broadband jammer denying GNSS to a nearby receiver.
scenarios.kindDesc: Link-budget jamming: J/S → effective C/N₀ → loss of lock.
scenarios.toml:
# RF jamming: a ground-based broadband jammer denying GNSS to a nearby receiver.
#
# The chain (Kaplan & Hegarty, Understanding GPS/GNSS, 3rd ed. §9.4): the jammer's
# received power (transmit power + gains − free-space path loss) sets the
# jammer-to-signal ratio J/S at the receiver; the despreading processing gain
# (C/A chip rate) and the spectral-separation factor Q convert that into an
# effective C/N0 per satellite; a satellite loses lock when its effective C/N0
# falls below the tracking threshold (25 dB-Hz here).
#
# A 10 W (10 dBW) broadband jammer 1 km from the receiver produces J/S ≈ 72 dB —
# far beyond the ~35 dB a C/A loop can tolerate — so every visible satellite drops
# below the tracking threshold and the receiver is denied (availability → 0) while
# the satellites remain geometrically visible. Move the jammer out or cut its
# power and J/S falls ~40 dB per decade of range: the same jammer at 100 km only
# degrades the links (J/S ≈ 32 dB, effective C/N0 ≈ 28 dB-Hz) without losing lock.
kind = "jamming"
seed = 1
mask_deg = 5.0
tracking_threshold_dbhz = 25.0

[time]
step_s = 30.0
duration_s = 1800.0

[receiver]
lat_deg = 52.0
lon_deg = 4.0
alt_m = 0.0

# A GPS-like 24-satellite Walker shell (6 planes × 4), propagated through the
# 4.12 mm-validated SGP4 core.
[constellation]
altitude_km = 20200.0
inclination_deg = 55.0
planes = 6
sats_per_plane = 4
phasing_f = 1.0

# 10 W broadband jammer 1 km East of the receiver (ECEF; J/S depends only on
# range, so the exact direction is immaterial).
[jammer]
position_ecef_m = [3926375.101, 274488.966, 5002803.345]
power_dbw = 10.0
gain_dbi = 0.0
jammer_type = "broadband"
bandwidth_mhz = 20.0

scenarios.desc: L-band waterfall under jamming: the whole Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) L band as one power spectral density (PSD), frequency across, time down, while a scripted sequence of jammers switches on.
scenarios.kindDesc: L-band spectrum model and waterfall: the whole GNSS L band as one power spectral density (PSD), frequency across, time down, over a scripted jammer timeline. SIGNALS: GPS L1 C/A and L2C (BPSK(1)), Galileo E1 open service (MBOC(6,1,1/11), or BOC(1,1)), GPS L5 and Galileo E5a (BPSK(10)), each at its carrier with the interface-specification minimum received power (IS-GPS-200, IS-GPS-705, Galileo OS SIS ICD) unless overridden; GLONASS, BeiDou and Galileo E6 are not modelled. JAMMERS: continuous-wave tone, flat narrowband noise, linear sawtooth chirp and broadband noise matched to a band's own modulation, each with a centre, a bandwidth, a received power (direct, or EIRP and range through the jamming kind's free-space path loss) and on/off times. Each jammer is scored against each band by its spectral separation coefficient kappa over the receiver bandwidth, and (C/N0)_eff = [1/(C/N0) + sum (J/S) kappa]^-1; for one jammer this equals the jamming kind's anti-jam equation with Q = 1/(R_c kappa), and the report carries that cross-check (and the jamming kind's representative-Q figure beside it). The noise floor is k T_sys with T_sys = T_ant + 290 K (F - 1). The waterfall averages each cell over its bin and its row (chirps exactly, whole sweeps plus the partial one; jammers switching mid-row by their duty), so the C/N0 timeline and the picture come from the same numbers; result.json carries the grid block-averaged in power, per-band C/N0 and J/S per row, and per jammer per band the SSC, Q, J/S, in-band J/S and steady C/N0. Optional [iq]: the model drawn as complex IQ at one instant, written to and read back from a SigMF recording (cf32_le or ci16_le), and compared with a Welch estimate. Optional [recording] (native builds): a real SigMF recording's Welch PSD beside the model. VALIDATED: the signal PSDs against the textbook main-lobe widths (BPSK(n) 2n x 1.023 MHz null to null; BOC(1,1) lobes centred at +/-1.023 MHz) and the spectral separation coefficients against their Parseval closed forms and Kaplan & Hegarty's Q = 1 (CW) and 1.5 (matched). MODELLED: jammer powers, timeline, front-end bandwidths, the continuous-spectrum (no code lines) treatment and the absence of AGC, blanking and antenna pattern.
scenarios.toml:
# L-band waterfall under jamming: the whole Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS)
# L band as one power spectral density (PSD), frequency across, time down, while a
# scripted sequence of jammers switches on.
#
# The question a spectrum monitor or a receiver designer asks: what does the band look
# like while this happens, and which signals does each jammer actually take away? The
# navigation signals sit about 20 dB below the thermal noise floor, so the picture shows
# the floor and the jammers; the per-band carrier-to-noise density (C/N0) bars show what
# despreading recovers. Each jammer is scored against each band by its spectral
# separation coefficient (SSC), the overlap of the two spectra over the receiver band
# (Betz 2001; Kaplan & Hegarty, Understanding GPS/GNSS, 3rd ed., section 9.4), so a
# jammer only hurts the bands its spectrum reaches.
#
# Timeline (60 s, one row per second):
#   10 s  a swept (chirp) jammer, 16 MHz wide around L1, a 9 microsecond sawtooth, the
#         shape of a car-cigarette-lighter privacy device: 50 mW (-13 dBW) at 100 m.
#         It takes GPS L1 coarse/acquisition (C/A) and Galileo E1 away together.
#   30 s  a continuous-wave (CW) tone exactly on the L1 carrier, 10 mW at 1 km. On C/A
#         it lands on the peak of the binary phase-shift keying (BPSK) spectrum; on
#         Galileo E1 it lands in the null of the multiplexed binary offset carrier (MBOC)
#         spectrum, so E1 recovers when the chirp stops at 40 s while C/A stays lost.
#   45 s  flat 2 MHz noise on the L2 carrier, received at -135 dBW: GPS L2 civil (L2C)
#         is degraded but keeps tracking.
# GPS L5 and Galileo E5a, at 1176.45 MHz, are outside every jammer's spectrum.
#
# The [iq] section draws the model at 35 s as complex IQ samples (20.48 MHz around L1),
# writes them as a Signal Metadata Format (SigMF) recording and reads them back, and
# compares a Welch estimate with the model: a check of the synthesis, the SigMF codec and
# the estimator, not a measurement. A real recording can be compared instead with a
# [recording] section (meta_path = "capture.sigmf-meta"), native builds only.
#
# Assumptions: signal powers are the interface-specification minimum received powers
# (IS-GPS-200, IS-GPS-705, Galileo Open Service Signal-in-Space Interface Control
# Document); a 290 K antenna and a 2 dB receiver noise figure; free-space propagation
# to the jammers, 0 dBi receive gain toward them. MODELLED: the signal spectra are
# validated closed forms, but every jammer, power and timing here is a scenario input.
kind = "spectrum"
seed = 7
duration_s = 60.0
step_s = 1.0

[receiver]
noise_figure_db = 2.0
antenna_temp_k = 290.0
tracking_threshold_dbhz = 25.0

[grid]
f_min_mhz = 1160.0
f_max_mhz = 1590.0
n_freq = 430

[[jammers]]
name = "chirp privacy device"
waveform = "chirp"
centre_mhz = 1575.42
bandwidth_mhz = 16.0
sweep_period_us = 9.0
eirp_dbw = -13.0
range_m = 100.0
on_s = 10.0
off_s = 40.0

[[jammers]]
name = "CW tone on L1"
waveform = "cw"
centre_mhz = 1575.42
eirp_dbw = -20.0
range_m = 1000.0
on_s = 30.0

[[jammers]]
name = "L2 narrowband noise"
waveform = "narrowband"
centre_mhz = 1227.60
bandwidth_mhz = 2.0
received_power_dbw = -135.0
on_s = 45.0

[iq]
centre_mhz = 1575.42
sample_rate_mhz = 20.48
t_s = 35.0
log2_samples = 16
nfft = 1024
datatype = "cf32_le"

scenarios.desc: LEO-PNT band trade, UHF to wide C band: what a low Earth orbit (LEO) positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) signal gains and loses in each band, independent of any particular system.
scenarios.kindDesc: LEO-PNT signal designs: parameterised low Earth orbit (LEO) positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) signals for any system, band and structure. A SIGNAL is a band (centre frequency, transmit bandwidth, ITU allocation RNSS/RDSS/MSS/EESS/non-RNSS/other) and components (acquisition, data, pilot; any subset), each with a modulation (BPSK(n) with fractional n, BOC(m,n), MBOC(6,1,p) or a flat OFDM-like band), a power share, optional FDMA sub-carrier offsets, a code length and a data rate. Signals come from compiled-in public preset files (xona-pulsar, iridium-stl, starlink-soo, centispace, generic-c-band, generic-bands; each with its source URL and every unpublished value labelled REPRESENTATIVE) or are written inline. PER SIGNAL: the band-limited power spectral density and the fraction of each component's power the transmit band passes (BPSK closed form beside the numeric value), the RMS (Gabor) bandwidth, the delay-lock-loop code-tracking thermal-noise jitter against C/N0 and early-late spacing from the band-limited coherent (or non-coherent) early-late formula of Betz & Kolodziejski 2009 with its unlimited-band textbook form and its vanishing-spacing Gabor bound, the ranging accuracy in metres, the acquisition search space (Doppler bins from the orbit's maximum Doppler plus oscillator and user terms, times code bins), square-law detection probability and the mean serial and code-parallel acquisition time, the spectral separation coefficient of the signal into GPS L1 C/A, Galileo E1, GPS L5, Galileo E5a, E5b and E5 AltBOC and of each into the signal with the C/N0 degradation, and the CW, wideband and matched J/S the tracked component tolerates, from the spectrum kind's own SSC machinery. A BAND TRADE: first-order ionospheric delay (40.3 TEC/f^2), free-space loss, ranging accuracy at equal C/N0 and at equal EIRP, and jammer tolerance. Optional SHAPE CHECKS hold a design's spectrum against a described measurement (MODELLED consistency). VALIDATED: the BPSK power-in-band (90.3 % in the main lobe) and Gabor-bandwidth closed forms, the band-limited jitter reducing to the textbook coherent early-late form and to its Gabor bound, the offset BPSK spectral separation coefficient against its Parseval closed form, the AltBOC spectrum's unit area, and the maximum LEO Doppler against the published Xona Pulsar (32-34 kHz) and Iridium (36 kHz) figures. MODELLED: every design, power split, C/N0 and jammer level; EFQPSK, CSK and OFDM spectra are approximated.
scenarios.toml:
# LEO-PNT band trade, UHF to wide C band: what a low Earth orbit (LEO) positioning,
# navigation and timing (PNT) signal gains and loses in each band, independent of any
# particular system.
#
# Five REPRESENTATIVE designs from the compiled-in `generic-bands` preset, each a pilot
# and data pair with a 50/50 power split sized to its band:
#   UHF   465 MHz,      BPSK(5) in 10 MHz
#   L     1191.795 MHz, BPSK(10) in 20.46 MHz (the Galileo E5 centre)
#   S     2492.028 MHz, BPSK(5) in 16.5 MHz (the NavIC S-band carrier, in the RDSS band)
#   C     5020 MHz,     BPSK(10) in 20 MHz (the middle of the 5010-5030 MHz RNSS band)
#   wide C 5100 MHz,    BPSK(50) in 120 MHz
# (BPSK binary phase-shift keying; RDSS Radio Determination Satellite Service; RNSS Radio
# Navigation Satellite Service.)
#
# The trade table puts four things side by side:
#   * ionospheric delay: first order, 40.3 TEC / f^2, for a 50 TECU slant total electron
#     content: UHF carries (1191.795/465)^2 = 6.6 times the L-band delay, C band 0.056;
#   * free-space loss at a 1000 km slant range: +20 log10(f/f_L) dB relative to L;
#   * ranging accuracy (delay-lock-loop thermal-noise jitter, 0.5 chip coherent
#     early-late spacing, 1 Hz loop) at equal C/N0 (45 dB-Hz for all), and at equal
#     radiated power (C/N0 falls with the free-space loss: isotropic antennas at both
#     ends, so the higher band's smaller receive aperture is charged in full);
#   * the J/S a CW tone, wideband noise and matched noise may reach before the tracked
#     pilot falls below 25 dB-Hz, at the equal-power C/N0.
# MODELLED: the closed forms are validated; the designs, the TEC, the range and the
# equal-power assumption are inputs. No rain or atmospheric loss (it matters at C band).
kind = "leo-signal"
presets = ["generic-bands"]

[receiver]
noise_figure_db = 2.0
antenna_temp_k = 290.0
cn0_dbhz = [30.0, 35.0, 40.0, 45.0, 50.0, 55.0]
reference_cn0_dbhz = 45.0
loop_bandwidth_hz = 1.0
integration_time_s = 0.02
correlator_spacings_chips = [1.0, 0.5, 0.2, 0.1]
reference_spacing_chips = 0.5
tracking_threshold_dbhz = 25.0

[acquisition]
altitude_km = 550.0
oscillator_ppm = 0.5
coherent_ms = 1.0
noncoherent = 1
pfa_cell = 1e-4

[trade]
reference_signal = "generic-l"
slant_tec_tecu = 50.0
slant_range_km = 1000.0

scenarios.desc: Positioning from LEO Doppler alone, over a generic LEO navigation constellation.
scenarios.kindDesc: Fused medium-Earth-orbit (MEO) and low-Earth-orbit (LEO) positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) over ANY constellations: each [[system]] is a GNSS preset of the constellation-design kind, a LEO preset (xona-pulsar, iridium-stl, starlink-sop, centispace, generic-c-band, the atomic-zero-clock ephemeris model, or another preset file, each in its own file with its sources marked PUBLIC, WORKSHOP or DERIVED), Walker shells or explicit element sets, with a carrier, a chip rate, a carrier-to-noise density (C/N0) envelope from the elevation mask to the zenith, a signal-in-space range error (SISRE), a Doppler sigma and a clock model (its own receiver clock, so the inter-system bias is estimated, or a known broadcast offset). Four modes. DOPPLER: batch Gauss-Newton positioning from range rate with analytic partials, clock-drift and optional velocity states and an optional height constraint, single- or multi-satellite, the error against window length, the Doppler, Doppler-rate and jerk envelope of each LEO system, and the single-pass along-track and cross-track accuracy against the cross-track offset (the cross-track error grows without bound as the pass goes overhead; a single pass also has a mirror solution across the ground track). A Doppler-only signal of opportunity (starlink-sop) runs here. JOINT: per-epoch weighted least-squares pseudorange fixes from GNSS alone, LEO alone and both, per-measurement sigmas from a delay-lock-loop thermal-noise model at C/N0 plus the SISRE (or a fixed sigma, so a signal model can feed them), the estimated inter-system biases, and PDOP/HDOP/VDOP against the number of LEO satellites added. POLAR: satellites in view and DOP against latitude for GNSS, LEO and both. TIMING: time transfer to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) from LEO satellites at a known position with a two-state clock filter whose process noise comes from the engine's oscillator classes, against C/N0 and the oscillator, and the IS-GPS-200 system-time-to-UTC expression; with [timing] trace = true every row also reports its time error and predicted sigma at every epoch. VALIDATED: the largest Doppler of an overhead-to-horizon pass against the published Iridium (up to 36 kHz) and Xona Pulsar X1 (32 to 34 kHz) figures. MODELLED: everything else; the DOP is checked against a hand-derived case, the fixes against their covariance, and the Doppler model against the range-acceleration identity.
scenarios.toml:
# Positioning from LEO Doppler alone, over a generic LEO navigation constellation.
#
# A receiver near Munich measures the Doppler shift of every satellite of a 258-satellite
# LEO navigation constellation (the public Xona Pulsar X1 signal table and constellation,
# arXiv:2509.19551; the split between its two inclinations is representative) for ten
# minutes and solves for its position and clock drift by batch least squares. Doppler gives
# range rate, and only the part of the satellite velocity across the line of sight carries
# position information, so the geometry is the change of the lines of sight over the pass,
# not the spread of satellites at one instant.
#
# The report gives the full-window error, the error against window length (how quickly a
# Doppler fix forms), the Doppler, Doppler-rate and jerk envelope of the system over an
# overhead pass, and a single-pass table: the formal along-track and cross-track errors of a
# fix from ONE satellite pass against the user's distance from the ground track. The
# cross-track error grows without bound as the pass goes overhead, where the Doppler curve
# stops depending on the cross-track distance (and the mirror image across the track fits
# almost as well).
#
# MODELLED. Doppler noise 1 Hz one sigma (0.19 m/s at 1593 MHz), perfect ephemeris, no
# ionosphere or troposphere rate, a height-free three-dimensional fit.
kind = "leo-pvt"
mode = "doppler"
seed = 7
duration_s = 600.0
step_s = 10.0

[user]
lat_deg = 48.14
lon_deg = 11.58
height_m = 520.0

[doppler]
pass_offsets_km = [25.0, 100.0, 250.0, 500.0, 1000.0, 1500.0]

[[system]]
name = "Pulsar X1"
leo_preset = "xona-pulsar"
signal = "X1"
sigma_doppler_hz = 1.0

scenarios.desc: LEO-PNT focus area: additional PNT data services in the navigation message.
scenarios.kindDesc: Campaign: existing scenario kinds composed into one run, with every number read from a real run of the named kind. Four sections, in any combination. PHASES: a chained mission on one shared timeline -- each phase runs one or more scenarios (for example jamming, then spoofing, then a clock in holdover with an inertial navigation system coasting beside it, then an integrity alarm, then recovery), their outputs are read into named channels (clock time error against its guard, carrier-to-noise density ratio against the tracking floor, protection level against the alert limit, position error, satellites tracking, alarm flags) by a per-kind preset or by explicit result paths, and resampled onto a common grid by zero-order hold, with phase boundaries and events; state is handed on by carry (a channel continues from the previous phase's end value), handoff (a previous phase's number written into this phase's scenario) and end_at (a phase ends at a time a run computed, such as a spoofing monitor's detection time). SWEEP: a grid over one to three dotted scenario keys of any kind (a whole-number segment indexes an array of tables, as in system.2.sisre_m), with metrics read by result path and, with runs above one, a seeded Monte Carlo ensemble at every node. MONTE_CARLO: realisation k runs at base_seed + k; each metric reports mean, standard deviation, nearest-rank 5th/50th/95th percentiles and a fixed-seed bootstrap 95% confidence interval on the mean. COMPOSE: several scenarios under shared values (one jammer's power and position written into a maritime and a road receiver), with a combined best/worst summary. The result carries a campaign hash, a digest over every member result, and a units entry for every emitted number; the interoperability exports write each member scenario that has geometry as its own file set. Composition identities are tested: a one-phase campaign reproduces the stand-alone run bit for bit, a fixed-seed ensemble is byte-stable, and on a white-frequency-noise clock the ensemble mean falls inside the reported interval with the spread matching sqrt(q_wf * tau). MODELLED: the additive carry and the zero-order hold are modelling choices, and each phase carries the label of the kind that ran it.
scenarios.toml:
# LEO-PNT focus area: additional PNT data services in the navigation message.
#
# A low Earth orbit (LEO) navigation message carries, besides the ephemeris and clock,
# service data: ionospheric corrections for single-frequency users (a Klobuchar-style set
# and a NeQuick-G-style set) and the system-time-to-UTC (Coordinated Universal Time)
# offset. Each service costs bits in every frame. The campaign composes four
# `leo-navmsg` encode-and-decode runs of the engine's documented Kshana LEO message frame
# (its own encoding modelled on the published message components, not any system's bit
# layout), from ephemeris and clock only to every service, and records the frame length
# and the ephemeris-and-clock share of it. A frame of B bytes takes 8*B/R seconds to
# broadcast at R bit/s, so each service's bytes are airtime on the data channel.
#
# Every frame is checked by the kind itself: a CRC-24Q (the 24-bit cyclic redundancy
# check of RTCM and SBAS) against its published check value, a decode round trip and a
# corrupted frame that must be rejected.
#
# MODELLED: bit counts of the Kshana frame; broadcast integrity flags and differential
# corrections beyond these services are not modelled.

title = "Navigation-message service data against frame length"
seed = 20260929

scenarios.toml:
# LEO-PNT focus area: MEO + LEO fused PNT.
#
# A receiver in Madrid fuses GPS, Galileo and the Xona Pulsar X5 signal (public signal
# table, arXiv 2509.19551; the inclined 1080 km shell) in one weighted least-squares
# pseudorange solution with an inter-system bias per system. How good must the LEO orbit
# and clock be for the LEO layer to help? The campaign sweeps the LEO signal-in-space
# range error (SISRE) from 5 cm to 5 m and records the root-mean-square (RMS) 3D error of
# the GNSS-only, LEO-only and fused solutions over half an hour, and the fused median
# position dilution of precision (PDOP).
#
# The GNSS-only solution does not change; the fused one approaches it when the LEO SISRE
# is metres and improves on it by the LEO geometry when the SISRE is decimetres: the
# broadcast-message and orbit-determination quality (see `leo-pnt-end-to-end`, which
# hands the navigation message's SISRE to this stage) decides whether fusing pays.
#
# MODELLED: stated per-system SISRE and loop noise from C/N0; no multipath.

title = "Fused MEO + LEO positioning against the LEO SISRE"
seed = 20260929

# LEO-PNT focus area: indoor navigation with UHF.
#
# Building entry loss grows with frequency, and modern thermally efficient buildings
# (metallised glass, foil-backed insulation) add far more than traditional ones. The
# campaign composes two `leo-pass` runs of one generic low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite

# carrier-to-noise density (C/N0) of each band.

PHASES: a chained mission on one shared timeline -- each phase runs one or more scenarios (for example jamming, then spoofing, then a clock in holdover with an inertial navigation system coasting beside it, then an integrity alarm, then recovery), their outputs are read into named channels (clock time error against its guard, carrier-to-noise density ratio against the tracking floor, protection level against the alert limit, position error, satellites tracking, alarm flags) by a per-kind preset or by explicit result paths, and resampled onto a common grid by zero-order hold, with phase boundaries and events; state is handed on by carry (a channel continues from the previous phase's end value), handoff (a previous phase's number written into this phase's scenario) and end_at (a phase ends at a time a run computed, such as a spoofing monitor's detection time). SWEEP: a grid over one to three dotted scenario keys of any kind (a whole-number segment indexes an array of tables, as in system.2.sisre_m), with metrics read by result path and, with runs above one, a seeded Monte Carlo ensemble at every node. MONTE_CARLO: realisation k runs at base_seed + k; each metric reports mean, standard deviation, nearest-rank 5th/50th/95th percentiles and a fixed-seed bootstrap 95% confidence interval on the mean. COMPOSE: several scenarios under shared values (one jammer's power and position written into a maritime and a road receiver), with a combined best/worst summary. The result carries a campaign hash, a digest over every member result, and a units entry for every emitted number; the interoperability exports write each member scenario that has geometry as its own file set. Composition identities are tested: a one-phase campaign reproduces the stand-alone run bit for bit, a fixed-seed ensemble is byte-stable, and on a white-frequency-noise clock the ensemble mean falls inside the reported interval with the spread matching sqrt(q_wf * tau). MODELLED: the additive carry and the zero-order hold are modelling choices, and each phase carries the label of the kind that ran it.
scenarios.toml:
# LEO-PNT focus area: low-energy positioning for the Internet of Things (IoT) and mobile.
#
# A battery-powered tag in Hamburg takes a hot-start fix from a generic low Earth orbit
# (LEO) UHF signal (465 MHz) during a 55 deg pass. How much transmit power does the
# satellite need for the tag to last? The campaign sweeps the UHF band's equivalent
# isotropically radiated power (EIRP) from -35 to +5 dBW and records, from the
# `leo-pass` kind's `[iot]` section, the median carrier-to-noise density (C/N0), the
# hot-start time to first fix (TTFF), the energy per fix and the battery life at one fix
# per hour (20 mW active, 5 microwatt asleep, 2000 mWh battery; all stated inputs).
#
# Higher received power shortens the acquisition dwell the receiver needs to reach its
# detection threshold, and energy per fix follows the time the receiver is awake. Below
# a median C/N0 of about 35 dB-Hz the receiver needs non-coherent sums and the energy per
# fix grows steeply; above it one coherent dwell suffices and the battery life at one fix
# per hour is set by the sleep current.
#
# MODELLED: acquisition, TTFF and energy from stated receiver assumptions; not a measured
# receiver. The UHF EIRP of the generic preset is representative, not a real system's.
kind = "campaign"
title = "IoT energy per fix against LEO UHF transmit power"
seed = 20260929

[sweep]
metrics = [
  { name = "uhf_median_cn0", path = "iot.rows[0].cn0_dbhz" },
  { name = "hot_ttff", path = "iot.rows[0].hot.ttff_s" },
  { name = "hot_energy_per_fix", path = "iot.rows[0].hot.energy_per_fix_mj" },
  { name = "battery_life_hourly", path = "iot.rows[0].duty_cycle_hot[4].battery_life_days" },
]

[[sweep.axes]]
name = "uhf_eirp"
key = "satellite.0.band.0.eirp_dbw"
unit = "dBW"
start = -35.0
stop = 5.0
steps = 9

[sweep.scenario]
kind = "leo-pass"
name = "IoT energy per fix"
epoch = "2026-09-28T06:00:00"
duration_s = 900.0
step_s = 10.0

[sweep.scenario.user]
environment = "ground"
lat_deg = 53.55
lon_deg = 9.99
height_m = 10.0

[[sweep.scenario.satellite]]
id = "LEO-1"
system = "generic-leo"
bands = ["UHF"]
max_elevation_deg = 55.0
tca_s = 450.0

[[sweep.scenario.satellite.band]]
name = "UHF"
eirp_dbw = 0.0

[sweep.scenario.gnss]
enabled = false

[sweep.scenario.iot]
active_power_mw = 20.0
sleep_power_uw = 5.0
battery_mwh = 2000.0
detection_snr_db = 16.0
max_coherent_ms = 20.0
parallel_code_search = true
aided_doppler_uncertainty_hz = 500.0
fix_intervals_s = [1.0, 10.0, 60.0, 600.0, 3600.0, 86400.0]
cn0_from = "median"

scenarios.toml:
# LEO-PNT focus area: 5G/6G non-terrestrial network (NTN) compatibility.
#
# A 5G NTN user terminal can position itself from the downlink of a low Earth orbit (LEO)
# NTN constellation: time of arrival (TOA) from the positioning reference signal, whose
# ranging precision is set by its bandwidth through the Cramer-Rao bound (CRB), and
# Doppler over a pass. The campaign sweeps the reference signal's occupied bandwidth from
# 180 kHz (one narrowband-IoT resource block, as in 5G NR NTN narrowband) to 20 MHz, in
# the S-band mobile-satellite-service (MSS) downlink around 2172.5 MHz, over a generic
# 324-satellite NTN shell at 600 km, and records the CRB range sigma at the zenith and the
# resulting root-mean-square 3D TOA position error.
#
# The range sigma falls as 1/(RMS bandwidth), about 6.5 m at the zenith for 180 kHz and
# 6 cm for 20 MHz; the 3D error falls from about 30 m to about 2 m, where the 1 m network
# synchronisation error (a scenario input) sets the floor.
#
# MODELLED: positioning from Cramer-Rao bounds with a stated synchronisation error; no
# multipath, no 3GPP (Third Generation Partnership Project) waveform detail beyond the
# bandwidth.
kind = "campaign"
title = "NTN positioning against reference-signal bandwidth"
seed = 20260929

[sweep]
metrics = [
  { name = "range_sigma_zenith", path = "signals[0].range_sigma_zenith_m" },
  { name = "toa_rms_error_3d", path = "signals[0].toa_rms_error_3d_m" },
  { name = "toa_availability", path = "signals[0].toa_availability" },
]

[[sweep.axes]]
name = "bandwidth"
key = "signal.0.bandwidth_hz"
unit = "Hz"
start = 180000.0
stop = 20000000.0
steps = 9
scale = "log"

[sweep.scenario]
kind = "ntn-positioning"
seed = 5
carrier_hz = 2172.5e6
integration_s = 0.1
doppler_integration_s = 1.0
cn0_dbhz = [38.0, 50.0]
sync_error_m = 1.0
duration_s = 600.0
step_s = 30.0

[sweep.scenario.user]
lat_deg = 52.5
lon_deg = 13.4
height_m = 40.0

[[sweep.scenario.signal]]
name = "NTN positioning reference signal"
bandwidth_hz = 4.5e6

[[sweep.scenario.system]]
name = "NTN shell"
role = "leo"
mask_deg = 10.0

[[sweep.scenario.system.shell]]
total = 324
planes = 18
phasing = 1
altitude_km = 600.0
inclination_deg = 55.0

scenarios.toml:
# LEO-PNT focus area: high-accuracy positioning (precise point positioning, PPP).
#
# Adding a low Earth orbit (LEO) layer shortens PPP convergence because the LEO geometry
# changes in minutes rather than hours, which separates the float ambiguities from the
# position quickly. The trade: a lower orbit changes geometry faster but puts fewer
# satellites in view. The campaign sweeps the altitude of a 192-satellite Walker layer
# (12 planes, 60 deg) at 500, 1000 and 1500 km over a multi-GNSS float PPP (GPS, Galileo,
# BeiDou and GLONASS, ionosphere-free code and phase) at one mid-latitude site, and
# records the median time for the horizontal and vertical errors to stay under 10 cm
# (six noise realisations per altitude, 30 s epochs, so times come in half minutes).
#
# Reference trend: Li et al. 2019 (J Geodesy, doi 10.1007/s00190-018-1195-2) simulated
# 60, 96, 192 and 288 LEO satellites at 1000 km cutting multi-GNSS convergence from 9.6
# to 7.0, 3.2, 2.1 and 1.3 min; `leo-ppp-convergence` compares the engine with that
# table. This sweep is a design study around it, not a reproduction.
#
# MODELLED: float PPP with white code and phase noise and a random-walk zenith wet
# delay; no ambiguity resolution, no multipath.
kind = "campaign"
title = "PPP convergence against the altitude of a 192-satellite LEO layer"
seed = 20260929

[sweep]
metrics = [
  { name = "gnss_only_convergence", path = "cases[0].median_convergence_min" },
  { name = "gnss_leo_convergence", path = "cases[1].median_convergence_min" },
  { name = "mean_sats_in_view", path = "cases[1].mean_sats" },
]

[[sweep.axes]]
name = "leo_altitude"
key = "case.0.system.0.shell.0.altitude_km"
unit = "km"
start = 500.0
stop = 1500.0
steps = 3

duration_s = 1800.0

runs = 6

lon_deg = 11.6

scenarios.desc: LEO-PNT focus area: LEO-PNT science, ionosphere sounding from the dual-band delay.
scenarios.kindDesc: LEO pass and link budget, band by band, for LEO-PNT (positioning, navigation and timing from low Earth orbit), system-agnostic: a user (ground, maritime, air or indoor, static or moving) and one or more LEO satellites from a DESIGNED PASS (a circular orbit placed so the user sees one pass of a chosen maximum elevation at a chosen time, sun-synchronous if asked), explicit ELEMENTS, a TLE (two-line element set) through the engine's SGP4, or a WALKER constellation built by the constellation-design code (the highest passes reported). Bands come from a named preset (generic multi-band UHF/L/S/C, generic C band, Xona Pulsar X1/X5, Iridium STL, Starlink as a Doppler-only signal of opportunity, CentiSpace, and an optional Celeste IOD preset marked WORKSHOP) or are written into the scenario; each preset states whether its numbers are PUBLIC (with URL), REPRESENTATIVE or WORKSHOP. Per satellite, band and epoch: elevation, azimuth, range, range rate and range acceleration; free-space path loss; EIRP and the satellite pattern gain (isoflux, Gaussian beam or flat); user antenna gain against elevation (patch, hemispherical or isotropic); gaseous attenuation (ITU-R P.676-10 Annex 2), rain attenuation (ITU-R P.838-3 coefficients and the P.618-14 procedure, from a rain rate and rain height), tropospheric scintillation (ITU-R P.618-14 section 2.4.1), building entry loss for an indoor user (ITU-R P.2109-2), polarisation mismatch, system noise temperature and C/N0 (carrier-to-noise density); Doppler and Doppler rate in closed form from the range rate and range acceleration, each checked against central differences; the first-order ionospheric delay 40.3 STEC/f^2 from a Klobuchar or vertical-TEC slant TEC scaled to the part of the ionosphere below the satellite. Band pairs get the ionosphere-free coefficients, noise amplification and code noise at the pass peak. MEO GNSS satellites (Galileo or GPS presets) are evaluated with the same antenna and noise model from their interface-document received powers, so the LEO bell-shaped pass and the flat GNSS carriers share one plot. An optional [iot] section gives time to first fix, energy per fix and battery life against duty cycle for a stated receiver power budget (MODELLED). Each band pair also gives the slant TEC its geometry-free combination recovers at the peak and that estimate's code-noise sigma (ionosphere sounding). An optional [spoofer] section counterfeits the signals of a claimed position that jumps or is pushed from the true one after an onset and runs two monitors with stated false-alarm and missed-detection probabilities: Doppler and pass-geometry consistency (measured range rates against those predicted from the orbits and an independent prior position and velocity, a generalised least-squares chi-square test over a window, on the GNSS, LEO and all channels) and cross-band consistency (the epoch-to-epoch step of each LEO band pair's model-corrected geometry-free combination), reporting per-epoch statistics and when each monitor detects (MODELLED). VALIDATED components: free-space loss, the P.838-3 coefficients against its Table 5, the P.618-14 rain and scintillation procedures and the P.2109 building entry loss against the ITU-R Study Group 3 validation examples, the IS-GPS-200 L1/L2 group-delay ratio, and the static-user maximum Doppler of a circular orbit against arXiv 2509.19551 Table 1. MODELLED: EIRPs, patterns, the Chapman fraction of TEC below the satellite and the whole pass.
scenarios.toml:
# LEO-PNT focus area: LEO-PNT science, ionosphere sounding from the dual-band delay.
#
# The first-order ionospheric group delay is 40.3*STEC/f^2 (STEC slant total electron
# content), so the difference of two bands' pseudoranges to one satellite measures the
# slant TEC below the satellite: STEC = (P2 - P1)*f1^2*f2^2 / (40.3*(f1^2 - f2^2)). A low
# Earth orbit (LEO) positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) satellite transmitting in
# several bands is therefore also an ionosphere sounder, and one below most of the
# plasmasphere: it sees only the electron content under its own altitude.
#
# One generic LEO satellite at 550 km passes 70 deg over the Tromso ionospheric
# observatory region (69.66 N) in UHF, L, S and C bands; the ionosphere is a 25 TEC-unit
# vertical content on a 350 km shell, scaled by the fraction of a Chapman layer below the
# satellite. For every band pair the report gives the slant TEC the geometry-free
# combination recovers at the pass peak and its 1-sigma from the two bands' code noise.
# Pairs with UHF sound best (UHF with L to about 0.02 TEC units): UHF carries the largest
# delay and, here, the strongest signal. The close S and C bands sound worst (about 3 TEC
# units): their delay difference is small against their code noise.
#
# MODELLED: the recovered TEC equals the model's by construction (the combination is exact
# at first order); the precision is the thermal code noise alone, without multipath or
# inter-frequency biases, which a real sounder must calibrate.
kind = "leo-pass"
name = "LEO ionosphere sounding from multi-band delays"
epoch = "2026-09-28T11:00:00"
duration_s = 900.0
step_s = 5.0

[user]
environment = "ground"
lat_deg = 69.66
lon_deg = 18.94
height_m = 20.0
mask_deg = 10.0

[ionosphere]
model = "vtec"
vtec_tecu = 25.0

[[satellite]]
id = "LEO-1"
system = "generic-leo"
bands = ["UHF", "L", "S", "C"]
max_elevation_deg = 70.0
tca_s = 450.0

[gnss]
constellation = "galileo"
band = "E1"

scenarios.toml:
# Indoor LEO-PNT: why a UHF carrier reaches inside a building when L, S and C bands struggle.
#
# A user inside a traditional building in Rome receives one pass of a generic multi-band LEO
# satellite (the representative generic-leo preset: UHF 450 MHz, L 1191.795 MHz, S 2492.028 MHz
# and C 5020 MHz, each 0 dBW EIRP, 550 km sun-synchronous) and the Galileo E1 carriers. The
# building entry loss is the ITU-R P.2109-2 median (probability 0.5) for a traditional
# building, evaluated at each satellite's elevation, which is also the elevation of the path
# at the facade. Outdoors, a 30 mm/h rain rate exceeded 0.01 % of the year (at a 3.5 km rain
# height) adds ITU-R P.618 rain attenuation, which matters at C band and not at UHF.
#
# UHF enters the building with several dB less loss than C band and loses less to free space
# at the same range, while its first-order ionospheric delay is about 125 times that at C band
# (the 1/f^2 law): the report lists both, and the ionosphere-free combination of each band pair
# with its noise amplification.
#
# MODELLED. The building model is statistical (ITU-R P.2109 is not site-specific); the EIRPs
# and beams are representative. No workshop data is used.
kind = "leo-pass"
name = "Indoor UHF LEO-PNT"
epoch = "2026-09-28T12:00:00"
duration_s = 900.0
step_s = 5.0

[user]
environment = "indoor"
lat_deg = 41.9
lon_deg = 12.49
height_m = 50.0
building = "traditional"
building_probability = 0.5
antenna = "hemispherical"
gain_dbi = 0.0
polarisation = "linear"

[atmosphere]
rain_rate_mm_h = 30.0
rain_height_km = 3.5
rain_exceedance_percent = 0.01

[ionosphere]
model = "vtec"
vtec_tecu = 30.0

[[satellite]]
id = "LEO-1"
system = "generic-leo"
bands = ["UHF", "L", "S", "C"]
max_elevation_deg = 60.0
tca_s = 450.0

[gnss]
constellation = "galileo"
band = "E1"

# LEO navigation message: Kshana's binary encoding, its quantisation budget, and the
# RINEX-style and CSV exports.
#
# The binary frame is Kshana's own documented encoding (preamble, version, model, length,
# payload, CRC-24Q). It carries the published components of a LEO message (a Galileo-

# error stays under a millimetre over the validity window. It is not the bit layout of
# any operational or demonstration system; none is public.

# CRC (and that a flipped bit is rejected), prints the per-field half-step budget and
# the SISRE of the exact and decoded message against the truth, then writes all three as
# a RINEX-4-style block (a documented Kshana extension: RINEX 4.02 has no LEO records;
# prior art arXiv 2401.17767) and as a CSV table, and reads both back.

name = "LEO message encode and decode"
seed = 14
analysis = ["encode-decode"]

altitude_km = 550.0
inclination_deg = 97.6
gravity_degree = 20

rac_degrees = [7, 5, 6]

update_period_s = 300

# LEO navigation message: signal-in-space range error (SISRE) versus fit interval.
#
# A low Earth orbit (LEO) positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) satellite broadcasts
# its orbit as a compact parameter set fitted to a short arc. The question: how long can
# one message cover before its representation error outgrows the target, and what does a
# set of along-track, cross-track and radial (RAC) correction polynomials buy?
#
# Truth: a 550 km, 97.6 deg orbit integrated with the EGM2008 gravity field to degree 20
# and drag. Each message is fitted over its interval and used over a period centred in
# it. Two models: the Galileo Open Service Signal-in-Space Interface Control Document
# (OS SIS ICD) 16-parameter Keplerian set, and that set plus RAC polynomials of degree
# 7 (along), 5 (cross) and 6 (radial). Why so high: the least-squares Keplerian residual
# is what the 16 parameters cannot span, so it oscillates across the window, and only a
# polynomial of higher degree than the Keplerian set already spans removes it (a
# cross-track polynomial of lower degree removes almost nothing). SISRE uses the
# global-average weights for the
# orbit altitude (Montenbruck et al. 2018 method): at 550 km the radial weight is about
# 0.47 and the transverse weight squared about 1/2.6, so along- and cross-track errors
# count far more than for medium Earth orbit.
#
# The first table sets the usage period equal to the fit interval (1 to 15 minutes);
# the second holds a 5-minute fit and shortens the update period. No preset is used: the
# numbers are Kshana's own truth and fit, the representation error only (no orbit
# determination or prediction error). MODELLED.
kind = "leo-navmsg"
name = "LEO message fit-interval trade"
seed = 11
analysis = ["fit-interval-trade"]

[orbit]
altitude_km = 550.0
inclination_deg = 97.6
gravity_degree = 20
cd_area_over_mass = 0.005

[message]
model = "kepler-rac"
rac_degrees = [7, 5, 6]

[trade]
span_s = 1800
fit_intervals_s = [60, 120, 180, 300, 450, 600, 900]
update_periods_s = [30, 60, 150, 300]
update_fit_interval_s = 300
models = ["kepler16", "kepler-rac"]

# LEO navigation message: a message update in the middle of a pass, and whether the user
# sees a jump.
#
# A LEO pass lasts minutes, so a satellite may switch to a new message while a user is
# tracking it. At each switch the user's modelled pseudorange changes by the difference

# FAIL against a 5 cm continuity threshold. A range-error series along the pass shows the
# message error itself around each switch. No preset; MODELLED.

# The Liu table fits Kshana's 22-parameter model over 20-minute arcs at the five
# altitudes of the paper (320, 475, 786, 966, 1336 km) and prints the published SISRE
# beside it. The paper fitted real precise science orbits of named satellites; Kshana
# fits its own integrated orbit at the same altitude and inclination, so the comparison
# is MODELLED, not VALIDATED.

# first-order ionosphere on each.

# MODELLED (workshop-calibrated). Not a measurement of any Celeste satellite.

name = "Celeste IOD multi-band pass"

# A LEO-PNT pass against the Galileo satellites in view: C/N0 over one pass.
#
# LEO-PNT is positioning, navigation and timing from satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO). A
# ground user near Munich watches one pass of a generic LEO navigation satellite (the
