scenarios.desc: Lunar-native RF jamming: per-satellite J/S for a lunar surface user.
scenarios.kindDesc: Lunar-native RF jamming: per-satellite jammer-to-signal ratio, effective C/N₀ and loss of lock for a selenographic surface user under a lunar surface (or raised) jammer, over the illustrative public-source Moonlight/LCNS-class lunar-orbit constellation. Composes the existing open jamming physics (jamming::j_over_s_db, effective_cn0_dbhz, rx_antenna_gain_db, lock_status, q_factor) with the existing lunar sky geometry (lunar_service::LunarConstellation + topocentric, lunar::selenographic_to_mcmf); no geometry or radiometry is re-derived. Unlike the Earth `jamming` kind, the signal leg is NOT a fixed received power: each satellite's isotropic received power is its own link budget EIRP − FSPL(slant range), so the J/S varies satellite by satellite with lunar range and elevation. Reports ONE ROW PER VISIBLE (epoch, satellite) LINK — azimuth, elevation, slant range, both received powers the J/S is the difference of, the J/S, the nominal and effective C/N₀ and the lock status — plus aggregate figures of merit beside (never in place of) that table, and the same table as a CSV artifact. Every emitted numeric field carries a unit and a provenance class. VALIDATED sub-results carry their source module oracle (the anti-jam equation and J/S link of Kaplan & Hegarty §9.4, externally referenced in tests/gnss_denied_jamming_resilience_reference.rs; the lunar geometry of lunar_service). The composition itself is cross-checked against an independent two-link-budget path (linkbudget::received_signal_power_dbw, a different free-space-loss expression) to 1e-9 dB. MODELLED: the illustrative constellation, the representative EIRP / jammer power / antenna gains / noise temperature, and the absence of terrain shadowing, multipath, AGC dynamics and adaptive nulling. Not a certified denial-of-service product. With a jammer configured the report also carries a DENIAL CONTOUR WITH AN UNCERTAINTY BAND rather than a contour read off one scalar: the full measured wanted-signal C/N₀ distribution over the per-satellite table (n, min, p05, p25, median, p75, p95, max, mean, sample stdev, and the sample's own asymmetry), and the contour evaluated at each of those order statistics under BOTH denial criteria the engine recognises — the incumbent power-ratio one (J/S = 30 dB, as in attack-surface and tracking-loop) and the loss-of-lock one (effective C/N₀ falling to tracking_threshold_dbhz, the criterion this report's own status column uses) — on both axes of the denial plane (required jammer EIRP at the scenario standoff, denial standoff at the scenario EIRP). The band edges ARE contour(p05) and contour(p95), the same closed-form map applied to the sample's own quantiles: not a sigma fitted to the sample and not median ± k·stdev, with stdev emitted for continuity and used by nothing. A quantile already at or below the tracking threshold has no finite denying J/S and its loss-of-lock columns are null with a counted reason, never a clamped radius.
scenarios.toml:
# Lunar-native RF jamming: per-satellite J/S for a lunar surface user.
#
# The `jamming` kind is Earth-shaped — it takes a Walker/SGP4 shell and a WGS-84
# geodetic receiver, so a lunar case could only be assembled outside the engine by
# running `link-budget` twice (once for the jammer leg, once for the satellite leg)
# and subtracting the two received powers by hand. This kind runs that subtraction
# inside the engine, per satellite, per epoch.
#
# It composes, and re-derives nothing:
#   * jamming::j_over_s_db, effective_cn0_dbhz, rx_antenna_gain_db, lock_status,
#     q_factor, nominal_cn0_dbhz, free_space_path_loss_db  (the interference chain),
#   * lunar_service::LunarConstellation + topocentric, lunar::selenographic_to_mcmf
#     (the lunar sky geometry: MCI -> MCMF, then az / el / slant range from a
#     selenographic surface user).
#
# Unlike the Earth kind, the signal leg is not a fixed received power: each
# satellite's isotropic received power is its own link budget,
# `sat_eirp_dbw - FSPL(slant range, carrier)`, so the J/S moves satellite by
# satellite with lunar range and elevation. The result is a TABLE — one row per
# visible (epoch, satellite) link — published as JSON and as `*.table.csv`. The
# aggregate figures of merit sit beside that table, never in place of it.
#
# Every field below is optional; the values shown are the defaults except for the
# jammer block. Run it with:  kshana scenarios/lunar-jamming.toml
#
# MODELLED. The constellation is the illustrative, public-source Moonlight/LCNS-class
# geometry (not the real ephemeris; no affiliation or endorsement implied), and the
# interference model is a link budget: no terrain shadowing of the jammer (a
# first-order effect in south-polar terrain), no multipath, no AGC near/far dynamics,
# no adaptive nulling, no acquisition-vs-tracking hysteresis.

kind = "lunar-jamming"

# --- constellation (illustrative LCNS-class; apolune over the south) ------------
n_sats = 4
sma_km = 9737.4          # R_moon + 8000 km
eccentricity = 0.6
inc_deg = 57.7
argp_deg = 90.0

# --- surface user (selenographic) ----------------------------------------------
site_lat_deg = -89.67    # Shackleton crater rim
site_lon_deg = 129.78
site_alt_m = 0.0

# --- epoch grid ------------------------------------------------------------------
horizon_hours = 12.0
step_min = 60.0
elev_mask_deg = 5.0

# --- signal leg (link-budget leg 2, evaluated per satellite) ---------------------
sat_eirp_dbw = 26.0            # representative lunar AFS EIRP
carrier_hz = 2.4e9             # S-band AFS carrier
chip_rate_hz = 1.023e6         # despreading processing gain
user_boresight_gain_dbi = 3.0  # J/S is invariant to this; it moves C/N0 only

# --- receiver ---------------------------------------------------------------------
temp_k = 290.0
tracking_threshold_dbhz = 25.0
degraded_margin_db = 6.0

# --- jammer (link-budget leg 1). Omit this whole block for a clean-sky baseline. --
# Placed directly by standoff here. Give `lat_deg` and `lon_deg` instead to place it
# selenographically, and its range and elevation come from the same lunar geometry
# the satellites use (on an airless body a distant surface jammer then lands below
# the local horizon, and the antenna pattern hands it the horizon gain).
#
# 25 km is chosen because it splits the table: part of the visible set holds on and
# part does not. A single median J/S over these rows classifies the whole set as
# lost, which is exactly the collapse this kind exists to avoid.
[jammer]
power_dbw = 10.0        # 10 W
gain_dbi = 0.0
range_m = 25000.0
el_deg = 0.0            # a surface jammer on the user's local horizon
jammer_type = "broadband"
bandwidth_mhz = 20.0

scenarios.desc: Lunar joint multi-technique OD + clock determination (a SIMULATED network).
scenarios.kindDesc: Modelled joint multi-technique lunar OD + clock batch estimator on a SIMULATED network: a Gauss-Newton snapshot fit that fuses Earth-baseline geodetic VLBI delays, lunar-local station↔satellite ranges and inter-satellite ranges to recover, together, a lunar surface station's 3-D position, a small constellation's positions and every asset's clock offset from an injected truth. The headline honest result — VLBI makes the station's full 3-D position observable where lunar-local ranging alone leaves a weakly-observed direction — is reported as the with-vs-without-VLBI station-error contrast. MODELLED simulated closed-loop recovery (truth shares the observation model), deterministic (seeded), NOT real-data validated; no force-model propagation inside the solver; no TRL/heritage/agency endorsement.
scenarios.toml:
# Lunar joint multi-technique OD + clock determination (a SIMULATED network).
#
# A single-epoch (snapshot) batch least-squares fit (src/lunar_combination.rs, on top of
# crate::batch_ls::gauss_newton) that FUSES three observation techniques to recover, together:
#   * a lunar surface station's 3-D position (NovaMoon-class, MCI metres),
#   * a small lunar constellation's per-satellite positions (MCI metres), and
#   * every asset's clock offset (station + each satellite, seconds).
#
# The three techniques:
#   1. Earth-baseline geodetic VLBI delays to the lunar station treated as the VLBI beacon
#      (reusing src/lunar_vlbi.rs, in geocentric inertial) — these make the station's FULL
#      3-D position observable;
#   2. lunar-local station<->satellite ranges (MCI Euclidean distance + the differenced clock
#      term scaled by c) — these tie the satellite positions and clock differences;
#   3. inter-satellite ranges (same form) — these tie the constellation's relative geometry.
#
# THE HEADLINE HONEST RESULT: lunar-local ranging alone leaves the station's position weakly
# observed along one direction (the range-only solve is ill-conditioned and the recovered
# station 3-D error is large). Adding the Earth-baseline VLBI delays makes the station's full
# 3-D position observable, and the recovered station error collapses to the metre level. The
# report runs the solve WITH and WITHOUT the VLBI legs on the same seed/truth and reports the
# station-observability improvement factor.
#
# Honesty: MODELLED simulated closed-loop recovery. An injected truth is mapped to synthetic
# observables through the SAME geometry model the solver inverts, seeded Gaussian noise is added,
# and the estimator recovers the injected truth within the noise. The oracle is internal
# consistency (truth recovery + NEES covariance realism), NOT real-data validation. There is no
# force-model propagation inside the solver — the satellites are fixed, distinct, illustrative
# points on a representative lunar orbit. No TRL, flight heritage or agency endorsement claimed.
kind = "lunar-joint-od-clock"

# Network size.
n_sat = 3     # constellation satellites
n_earth = 6   # Earth ground stations (more stations -> more independent VLBI baselines and
              # better Earth->sat radiometric multilateration geometry)

# Deterministic seed (measurement noise + truth jitter).
seed = 42

# Per-observable measurement noise standard deviations (weights = 1/sigma^2). Illustrative,
# representative of the modelled class (geodetic VLBI, coherent two-way + optical ISL ranging).
sigma_vlbi_s = 1.0e-11   # VLBI delay sigma (s) ~ 3 mm path length
sigma_range_m = 0.1      # radiometric / lunar-local range sigma (m)
sigma_isl_m = 0.1        # inter-satellite (optical) range sigma (m)

# Lunar surface station (south-polar NovaMoon-class site), selenographic.
station_lat_deg = -88.0
station_lon_deg = 23.0
station_alt_m = 0.0

# Representative constellation orbit radius (km, MCI) the illustrative fixed satellites sit on.
orbit_radius_km = 6000.0

# Snapshot epoch (UTC).
epoch_year = 2024
epoch_month = 1
epoch_day = 1

scenarios.desc: Seven-parameter Helmert lunar frame datum from a REAL, ARCHIVED observing campaign (V3).
scenarios.kindDesc: Seven-parameter Helmert lunar frame datum driven by a REAL, ARCHIVED observing campaign rather than a simulated one. Where lunar-frame-campaign removed the injected transform but still stated its station network, its schedule and its per-observation sigma as ILLUSTRATIVE inputs, this kind takes all three from measurement: the epochs are the ground-transmit times of archived ILRS Consolidated Laser Ranging Data normal points, the observations are the laser ranges really fired at the five retroreflector arrays on the Moon, and every observation weight is that normal point's own archived precision bin_rms/sqrt(n_raw) read out of the file. Station coordinates come from the IERS ITRF2020 SLR solution (propagated to epoch by their published velocities) and the reflector coordinates from JPL DE430 Table 7 in the mean-Earth/mean-rotation frame the IAU 2015 WGCCRE model realises. Range partials accumulate into the joint reflector-coordinate Fisher information matrix and propagate through the same Helmert design into the datum covariance, diagnosed by crate::fim::crlb. Rank, defect, condition, spectrum, unobservable directions in the seven-parameter basis, the weakest direction at full rank and each parameter's share of it are emitted on every run, and an unconstrained parameter is published as NULL with a status. Inter-array correlation is MEASURED at exactly zero rather than assumed, because a laser range touches one array. A record the catalogues cannot place — a station with no published ITRF position — is SKIPPED AND COUNTED, never given a substituted coordinate. WHICH LINKS ARE MEASURED AND WHICH ARE MODELLED IS THE REPORT, NOT A FOOTNOTE: the Moon-centre ephemeris and the IAU body orientation remain modelled and their combined size is emitted as the observed-minus-computed one-way range residual over every point used; troposphere, solid-body tides, station eccentricity, polar motion, UT1-UTC, relativistic delay and station clocks are absent and inside that residual. Because an ephemeris error reaches a covariance only through the direction of each line of sight, every run also re-solves the whole datum with all partials tilted by sensitivity_tilt_deg (sign alternating) and emits the ratio, so the covariance's insensitivity to the modelled ephemeris is a number rather than an argument. The simulated campaign's own figures are RUN and printed beside the measured ones, not transcribed. MODELLED: the seven-parameter figures are a Cramer-Rao bound for a reduced parameter set on a real schedule — not a solved datum, not an LLR analysis and not a geodetic product. The committed real-data slice ships with the repository but not with the published crate; point data_dir at a copy of it.

scenarios.desc: A lunar relay and navigation constellation: satellites in elliptical lunar frozen orbits (ELFO) plus a circular low-lunar-orbit shell, scored as a coverage and dilution-of-precision (DOP) map over the whole Moon for one day.
scenarios.kindDesc: Constellation design at scale: Walker DELTA and Walker STAR patterns in the i: T/P/F convention (nodes spread over 360 or 180 deg, in-plane spacing 360*P/T, inter-plane phase offset 360*F/T), explicit element lists and multi-shell designs, several constellations in one run, around the Earth, the Moon, Mars or any other planet, Pluto or major moon using the constants in the body module (the same ones the solar-system and body-pnt kinds use). PRESETS from published nominal elements: gps-baseline and gps-expandable (the 24 slots and the six fore/aft expandable pairs of the GPS Standard Positioning Service Performance Standard, 5th edition 2020, Tables 3.2-1 to 3.2-3), galileo (Walker 24/3/1 at 29 599.801 km and 56 deg, Galileo Open Service Service Definition Document issue 1.1 Tables 1 and 23), beidou and beidou-meo (Walker 24/3/1 at 21 528 km and 55 deg plus three geostationary satellites at 80, 110.5 and 140 deg E and three inclined geosynchronous satellites at 55 deg, BeiDou Open Service Performance Standard 3.0 section 4.1; the MEO phase and the 118 deg E inclined-geosynchronous crossing are modelled because the standard does not state them) and glonass (24/3/1 at 19 100 km and 64.8 deg from the slot formula of the GLONASS Interface Control Document edition 5.1 section 5.2). COVERAGE AND DILUTION OF PRECISION: over a latitude/longitude grid and a sampled window with an elevation mask, the number of satellites in view, GDOP, PDOP, HDOP and VDOP per cell, the availability (a fix with PDOP at or below a threshold, 6 by default) per cell, globally (area-weighted) and at the worst site, with one receiver clock per constellation unless clock = "common". It scales to thousands of satellites: visibility is a dot product against each satellite's coverage half-angle, and satellites are banded by sub-satellite latitude each epoch so a grid row tests only those that can be in view; the report counts the pair tests saved. The JSON carries the grid maps and downsampled per-satellite ground tracks. VALIDATED: the Walker generator against Galileo OS SDD Table 23 and the GLONASS ICD slot formula, the GPS preset against the published equatorial-crossing column of SPS PS Table 3.2-1, and the GPS baseline global HDOP distribution against SPS PS Appendix B (median 0.94, 95% 1.25, mean 0.96, tolerance 0.03). MODELLED: two-body orbits with optional secular J2, a spherical body, geometric visibility only (no signal power, health or terrain), and the relative phase between different systems, which is not a snapshot of any real date.
scenarios.toml:
# A lunar relay and navigation constellation: satellites in elliptical lunar frozen orbits
# (ELFO) plus a circular low-lunar-orbit shell, scored as a coverage and dilution-of-precision
# (DOP) map over the whole Moon for one day.
#
# The central body is the Moon: gravitational parameter, 1 737.4 km radius and spin rate come
# from the body module (the DE and IAU values cited there). The design is illustrative, not
# any agency's:
#   - an ELFO shell: 8 satellites as a Walker 8/4/1 with perilune about 720 km and apolune
#     about 7 500 km (semi-major axis 5 847.4 km, eccentricity 0.58), 57.8 deg inclination
#     and argument of perilune 90 deg, so every satellite lingers at apolune over the south
#     polar region;
#   - a circular shell: 6 satellites as a Walker 6/3/1 at 1 500 km and 85 deg.
#
# One receiver clock is shared (clock = "common"): the relay set is one system on one time
# scale. Latitude is lunar body-fixed; the map is an equirectangular projection with no land
# outline.
#

scenarios.desc: Coordinated Lunar Time (LTC) end-to-end time-error budget over a tau grid.
scenarios.kindDesc: MODELLED end-to-end Coordinated Lunar Time (LTC) time-error budget: the seven LTC error terms assembled as time-error curves x_i(τ) over a whole averaging-time grid, root-summed into x_Σ(τ), and the clock-vs-frame CROSSOVER τ at which the growing clock term overtakes the constant real-time frame-realisation term (below it the budget is frame-limited, above it clock-limited) — the honest answer to the single-τ artifact. The τ-slopes are closed-form and analytically checkable (clock τ^{+1/2}/τ^{+1}, floors τ^0, measurement τ^{-1/2}) and the clock rows reproduce the published one-day clock specs (crate::clock_specs); the RF/optical-link, frame-realisation, relativistic-residual and ephemeris floor MAGNITUDES are Modelled budget allocations (documented defaults, caller-overridable), not measurements. The contribution is the reproducible crossover τ, not a certified per-term number; not certified for operational timekeeping.
scenarios.toml:
# Coordinated Lunar Time (LTC) end-to-end time-error budget over a tau grid.
#
# A single averaging-time (tau) error table invites the objection "you picked the tau that
# flatters your clock." This scenario answers it: the seven LTC error terms are assembled as
# time-error curves x_i(tau) (seconds) across a whole grid of averaging times, root-summed into
# x_Sigma(tau), and the clock-vs-frame CROSSOVER tau is located — the tau at which the growing
# clock term overtakes the constant real-time frame-realisation term. Below the crossover the
# budget is frame-limited (the reference-frame realisation dominates, not the clock); above it the
# clock dominates. Where the crossover falls depends entirely on the clock class — for the default
# passive H-maser it is far out in tau, for a coarse mini-RAFS it is seconds — which is exactly why
# a single-tau number is misleading. (src/lunar_time_budget.rs)
#
# Honesty: MODELLED. The tau-slopes are closed-form and analytically checkable (clock tau^{+1/2}
# or tau^{+1}, floors tau^0, measurement tau^{-1/2}) and the clock rows reproduce the published
# one-day clock specs; but the RF/optical-link, frame-realisation, relativistic-residual and
# ephemeris floor MAGNITUDES are Modelled budget allocations (documented defaults, caller-
# overridable), not measurements. The contribution is the reproducible crossover tau, not a
# certified per-term number. Nothing here is certified for operational timekeeping.
kind = "lunar-time-budget"

# On-board clock class driving the (growing) clock term. One of:
#   optical-master | passive-h-maser | rafs | mini-rafs
clock = "passive-h-maser"

# The averaging-time (tau) grid is the default 1 s ... 1e7 s log-spaced grid (8 points/decade).
# Uncomment to override:
# tau_min_s = 1.0
# tau_max_s = 1.0e7
# points_per_decade = 8

scenarios.desc: Lunar coordinate time (LTC/TCL): the relativistic Earth-Moon clock rate.
scenarios.kindDesc: Modelled relativistic Earth–Moon clock rate (Lunar Coordinate Time, LTC/TCL): the secular LTC−TT rate from the self-potential difference and the Moon's kinetic term, reported with the published 56–59 µs/day band, plus the accumulated offset over a horizon.
scenarios.toml:
# Lunar coordinate time (LTC/TCL): the relativistic Earth-Moon clock rate.
#
# A clock on the lunar surface ticks faster than an Earth-geoid (TT) clock. A
# first-principles post-Newtonian identity (src/lunar_time.rs) sums two named terms:
#   - self-potential difference: the IAU L_G geoid potential (W0 = L_G*c^2) minus the
#     Moon's surface self-potential GM_moon/R_moon -> the dominant ~ +57.5 us/day; and
#   - kinetic (second-order Doppler): -<v^2>/2c^2 from the geocentric Moon velocity
#     (finite-differenced from the Montenbruck-Gill lunar series) -> ~ -0.5 us/day.
# The total secular rate ~ 57 us/day is reported with the published 56-59 us/day band.
#
# Honesty: MODELLED, not certified. The headline us/day figure is reference-dependent
# (Earth geoid W0 vs a lunar selenoid, the time-averaging window, neglected sub-us/day
# centrifugal/J2 corrections) -> a band, not a single number, is the honest output.
# Nothing here is validated to sub-nanosecond absolute accuracy or certified for
# operational timekeeping. The report also gives the accumulated LTC-TT offset over the
# horizon and supports an inverse-variance ensemble (a minimal lunar paper-clock).
kind = "lunar-time-offset"

epoch_year = 2000    # LTC origin epoch (UTC); rate varies < 1e-3 us/day over the J2000 era
epoch_month = 1
epoch_day = 1
horizon_days = 1.0   # accumulate the LTC-TT offset over one day (~57 us)

scenarios.desc: Lunar geodetic VLBI: an Earth baseline observing a lunar-surface beacon.
scenarios.kindDesc: Modelled lunar geodetic VLBI delay observable: an Earth baseline (two ground stations, GCRS) observes a one-way signal from a NovaMoon-class lunar-surface beacon. Emits the near-field two-range-difference delay, its rate, and the wavefront-curvature near-field correction over a pass — cross-checked against the same-codebase plane-wave Δ-DOR observable in the far-field limit, with finite-difference-verified partials. MODELLED, NOT validated against real VLBI data; carries the frame-consistency, xp=yp=0 polar-motion and plane-wave-vs-near-field caveats.
scenarios.toml:
# Lunar geodetic VLBI: an Earth baseline observing a lunar-surface beacon.
#
# Two ground stations (a VLBI baseline, here a Goldstone-like and a Canberra-like site)
# observe a one-way signal from a NovaMoon-class transmitter on the lunar near side. The
# geodetic observable (src/lunar_vlbi.rs) is the NEAR-FIELD two-range difference
#   tau_geom = (|r2 - r_B| - |r1 - r_B|) / c
# (the Moon is near-field, not a plane wave), plus the station clock-offset difference and a
# differenced Earth-potential Shapiro term. The report gives the delay, its finite-difference
# rate, and the wavefront-curvature near-field correction over the pass, with partials
# available for OD/frame work.
#
# Oracle: in the far-field limit the geometric delay collapses to the same-codebase plane-wave
# delta-DOR observable (src/radiometric.rs), matched to machine precision; the partials are
# finite-difference checked. At true lunar distance the near-field correction is a non-zero
# tens-to-hundreds-of-microseconds term.
#
# Honesty: MODELLED, NOT validated against real VLBI data. Polar motion is dropped
# (xp = yp = 0) so station inertial positions carry a few-metre frame error; the beacon mixes
# a mean-equator-of-date Moon series with an ICRF body-fixed offset (jd_tdb ~ jd_tt), a
# frame-consistency mismatch below model fidelity; no light-time iteration, media or aberration
# beyond the differenced Shapiro. No TRL, flight heritage or agency endorsement is claimed.
kind = "lunar-vlbi"

# Station 1 (DSN Goldstone-like, California).
station1_lat_deg = 40.4256
station1_lon_deg = -116.8893
station1_alt_m = 1000.0

# Station 2 (DSN Canberra-like, Australia) — a long intercontinental baseline.
station2_lat_deg = -35.4014
station2_lon_deg = 148.9819
station2_alt_m = 688.0

# Beacon on the lunar near side (equatorial, sub-Earth point).
beacon_lat_deg = 0.0
beacon_lon_deg = 0.0
beacon_alt_m = 0.0

# Epoch (UTC) and pass sampling.
epoch_year = 2024
epoch_month = 1
epoch_day = 1
horizon_hours = 6.0
step_min = 30.0

scenarios.desc: Lunar-VLBI station-coordinate covariance from an explicit observing schedule (G8, paper D3).
scenarios.kindDesc: Lunar-VLBI station-coordinate covariance: the delay partials of the lunar-vlbi observable accumulated over an explicit SCHEDULE (baselines x epochs) into a Fisher information matrix, inverted, and reported as the station coordinate covariance and the per-coordinate station sigma — a computed engine output rather than a scalar delay precision pushed through an assumed isotropic g = 3 equipartition factor. The state carries Earth-FIXED (ITRS) station coordinates, so the Jacobian is the inertial partial rotated by each epoch's GCRS->ITRS matrix: Earth rotation is what makes those coordinates observable, and the report MEASURES the Earth-fixed line-of-sight sweep and the beacon declination rather than assuming them. One observation is one (baseline, epoch) pair with BOTH stations above the elevation mask, weighted 1/delay_sigma_s^2. Reports rank, datum defect, condition number, the full information spectrum, the covariance matrix, per-station per-axis and 3-D sigmas, and the free-network null space on every run; under a rank deficiency the headline sigma is published as NULL with a status, never read out of a near-singular inverse. The equipartition value c*delay_sigma_s*sqrt(g/N) for the SAME schedule is emitted beside the computed value with the ratio, together with the isotropic trace bound sqrt(p/trace(M)) that AM-HM makes a hard floor — so the ratio is the anisotropy the assumption discarded. The delay closure tau_ik = tau_ij + tau_jk makes only n-1 of the n(n-1)/2 baselines geometrically independent; the report states both counts. MODELLED: the Moon-centre ephemeris, station clocks, troposphere and Earth-orientation parameters are held FIXED and observations are treated as independent, so the covariance is a Cramer-Rao bound for a reduced parameter set, not a predicted session result; the delay sigma, station coordinates and schedule are inputs. The partial the geometric-delay Jacobian leaves out (the differenced Shapiro term) is measured by finite difference and emitted. Not a geodetic product.
scenarios.toml:
# Lunar-VLBI station-coordinate covariance from an explicit observing schedule (G8, paper D3).
#
# D3's published chain goes from a per-observation delay precision to a station coordinate
# uncertainty through an assumed ISOTROPIC equipartition factor g = 3. That step is the one
# the paper's own abstract calls modelled rather than measured. This scenario removes it:
# the lunar-VLBI delay partials are accumulated over a real schedule of (baseline x epoch)
# pairs into a Fisher information matrix, inverted, and reported as the station coordinate
# covariance — so the station sigma is an engine output.
#
# The state carries Earth-FIXED (ITRS) coordinates, so the Jacobian is the inertial partial
# rotated by each epoch's GCRS->ITRS matrix: Earth rotation is what makes those coordinates
# observable at all, and the report MEASURES the Earth-fixed line-of-sight sweep and the
# beacon declination rather than assuming them. One observation is one (baseline, epoch)
# pair with BOTH stations above the elevation mask, weighted 1/delay_sigma_s^2.
#
# What to read in the report
#   * per-station per-axis and 3-D sigmas — the computed answer;
#   * the equipartition value c*delay_sigma_s*sqrt(g/N) for the SAME schedule, printed
#     beside it with the ratio. That ratio IS the anisotropy the assumption discarded, and
#     the isotropic trace bound sqrt(p/trace(M)) makes AM-HM a hard floor, so the
#     assumption can only ever understate;
#   * rank, datum defect, condition number, the full spectrum and the free-network null
#     space, on every run. Under a rank deficiency the headline sigma is published NULL
#     with a status, never read out of a near-singular inverse;
#   * both baseline counts: delay closure tau_ik = tau_ij + tau_jk leaves only n-1 of the
#     n(n-1)/2 baselines geometrically independent.
#
# MODELLED: the Moon-centre ephemeris, station clocks, troposphere and Earth-orientation
# parameters are held FIXED and observations are treated as independent, so this is a
# Cramer-Rao bound for a reduced parameter set, not a predicted session result. The
# omitted differenced-Shapiro partial is measured by finite difference and emitted.
# Not a geodetic product.
#
# Every field below is the module default, written out so the run is reproducible from
# this file alone. Delete any line to fall back to the same value.

kind = "lunar-vlbi-fim"

scenarios.desc: Maritime port approach with GNSS jammed: how long an inertial navigation system (INS) keeps a ship inside the harbour-approach accuracy budget once the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) is lost.
scenarios.kindDesc: INS/TRN coasting error model: position error against coast duration, built from IMU coefficients rather than swept as an assumed drift rate. Five growth contributions, each with its own power of time — accelerometer bias (t²), gyro-bias tilt through gravity (t³), velocity random walk (t^1.5), angle random walk (t^2.5) and scale factor against travelled distance (t¹ cruising, t² under sustained specific force) — combined under a STATED rule (root-sum-square by default, or linear-sum, or deterministic-sum with stochastic-rss; all three are computed on every run so the choice is visible rather than buried). The coast durations reaching caller-supplied position thresholds (10 m and 50 m by default) are located by the engine's existing bisection, each with a per-contribution breakdown naming the dominant source, and each single contribution's crossing is additionally inverted algebraically so the two agree. A terrain-relative-navigation mode bounds the coast with periodic position fixes and reports the largest fix interval that holds each threshold; a position-only fix leaves velocity error and tilt alive across the fix, so it does not always bound the coast at any fix rate, and the report says so rather than returning a zero. MODELLED: the IMU class coefficients are representative band figures, not a datasheet, and the terrain-fix residual is an input. An unreached threshold is reported as null with a status, never as a zero. Not a certified inertial-navigation performance product.
scenarios.toml:
# Maritime port approach with GNSS jammed: how long an inertial navigation system
# (INS) keeps a ship inside the harbour-approach accuracy budget once the Global
# Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) is lost.
#
# The mission question: a vessel fitted with an INS enters a harbour approach at
# 12 knots (6.17 m/s) when GNSS is jammed (see `maritime-strait-jamming.toml` for why).
# How many seconds of free-inertial coast does it have before its position error passes
# 10 m, and before it passes 100 m? Those are the two accuracy figures that
# International Maritime Organization (IMO) Resolution A.1046(27), on the World-Wide
# Radionavigation System, gives for harbour entrances and approaches (10 m, 95 %) and
# for ocean waters (100 m, 95 %). They are used here as budgets, not as a claim of
# compliance.
#
# The model is `ins-trn-coast`: five growth terms (accelerometer bias, gyro-bias tilt
# through gravity, velocity random walk, angle random walk and scale factor times the
# distance run), combined root-sum-square and searched for the crossing times. The IMU
# (inertial measurement unit) is the representative navigation-grade class from the
# engine's grade table (Groves 2013, Table 4.1 band), the class of INS fitted to naval
# and high-end offshore vessels. It is NOT a datasheet for any product. Change
# `imu_grade` to "tactical" or "industrial" to see how a cheaper unit shortens the coast.
#
# Honest scope: most merchant ships carry no INS; they dead-reckon on a gyrocompass and
# a speed log, which this engine does not model. No terrain or radar aiding is applied
# (`trn_fix_mode = "none"`), so this is the unaided coast. MODELLED: every figure is
# modelled from class coefficients, not measured on a vessel.
kind = "ins-trn-coast"

imu_grade = "navigation"

# 12 knots, a typical harbour-approach speed. The scale-factor term grows with the
# distance run, so speed is part of the error model.
speed_m_s = 6.17
ref_accel_m_s2 = 0.0

combination = "rss"

# IMO A.1046(27) harbour-approach and ocean-waters figures, used as budgets (m).
crossing_thresholds_m = [10.0, 100.0]

drift_band_lo_m_per_s = 0.001
drift_band_hi_m_per_s = 0.050

# No aiding: the free-inertial coast over the whole approach.
trn_fix_mode = "none"

# A one-hour approach and berthing window.
mission_duration_s = 3600.0

scenarios.desc: Maritime GNSS spoofing: detecting a transmitter that drags a ship's reported position.
scenarios.kindDesc: Combined RF/measurement spoof detector (multi-SV RAIM-consistency + AGC + SQM, fused) vs a parameterised attack (power advantage, carrier-phase alignment, time/position push; TEXBAT-style).
scenarios.toml:
# Maritime GNSS spoofing: detecting a transmitter that drags a ship's reported position.
#
# The mission question: a spoofer near a shipping lane broadcasts counterfeit Global
# Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) signals slightly stronger than the real ones and
# pulls the ship's position fix several hundred metres off its true track. Position
# spoofing affecting ships has been publicly reported, for example vessels whose
# reported positions appeared on land; this file describes that pattern generically and
# models no particular incident. Would the receiver's own monitors catch it?
#
# The pack runs the combined spoof detector (`spoof-detect`): receiver autonomous
# integrity monitoring (RAIM) parity across satellites, automatic gain control (AGC)
# power monitoring and signal quality monitoring (SQM) of correlation distortion, fused
# into one decision. The attack is described in the parameters of the public TEXBAT test
# battery (Humphreys et al., ION GNSS 2012): the spoofer's power advantage, whether it
# is carrier-phase aligned, and whether it pushes position (a subset of satellites,
# visible to RAIM) or time.
#
# Here: a +2 dB power advantage (under the 3 dB AGC margin, so power alone misses it),
# not carrier aligned, pushing four satellites to drag the fix by 500 m. Try
# `carrier_aligned = true`, `push = "time"` and a smaller `power_advantage_db` to see
# the hard case that defeats these receiver-level layers.
#
# Honest scope: parameterised receiver observables, not raw signal samples; Kshana is a
# simulator, not a receiver. MODELLED: every figure is modelled, not validated against
# recorded maritime spoofing.

kind = "spoof-detect"

[attack]
power_advantage_db = 2.0
carrier_aligned = false
push = "position"
push_magnitude_m = 500.0
num_biased = 4
el_imbalance = 0.12

[detector]
sat_power_dbm = -130.0
agc_margin_db = 3.0
sqm_tolerance = 0.10
raim_p_fa = 1.0e-3
sigma_m = 5.0
fusion_threshold = 0.5

scenarios.desc: Maritime GNSS jamming: a shore- or vessel-borne broadband jammer denying the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) to a ship crossing open water.
scenarios.kindDesc: Link-budget jamming: J/S → effective C/N₀ → loss of lock.
scenarios.toml:
# Maritime GNSS jamming: a shore- or vessel-borne broadband jammer denying the Global
# Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) to a ship crossing open water.
#
# The mission question a ship's navigator or a coastal authority asks: how far across
# the water does a modest jammer take GNSS away? Over the sea there is no terrain or
# clutter between the jammer and the ship's antenna, so free-space path loss is the
# only thing that weakens the jammer, and a low-power device reaches a long way.
# Widespread GNSS interference affecting shipping has been publicly reported in several
# sea areas; this file does not model any particular incident.
#
# The chain is the one in `jamming-demo.toml` (Kaplan & Hegarty, Understanding GPS/GNSS,
# 3rd ed., §9.4): jammer received power sets the jammer-to-signal ratio J/S, despreading
# and the spectral-separation factor turn it into an effective carrier-to-noise density
# C/N0 per satellite, and a satellite is lost below the 25 dB-Hz tracking threshold.
# Here a 50 W (17 dBW) broadband jammer on a 30 m mast sits 30 km from a ship at sea
# level. Free-space loss over 30 km at the L1 frequency (1575.42 MHz) is about 126 dB,
# which leaves a mean J/S of about 48 dB, well past the roughly 35 dB a coarse/acquisition (C/A)
# code tracking loop tolerates, so the receiver loses every satellite. Move the jammer
# out or cut its power to find the range at which tracking returns (J/S falls about
# 20 dB per decade of range).
#
# Assumptions: 0 dBi jammer and ship antennas toward each other (a ship's GNSS antenna
# is not a controlled-reception pattern antenna (CRPA)), free-space propagation with no
# sea-surface multipath, a GPS-like 24-satellite Walker shell. The receiver position is
# a generic point in the northern Baltic Sea. MODELLED: every figure is modelled, not
# validated against measured maritime interference.
kind = "jamming"
seed = 1
mask_deg = 5.0
tracking_threshold_dbhz = 25.0

[time]
step_s = 30.0
duration_s = 1800.0

[receiver]
lat_deg = 59.80
lon_deg = 24.90
alt_m = 0.0

# A GPS-like 24-satellite Walker shell (6 planes x 4), propagated through the SGP4 core.
[constellation]
altitude_km = 20200.0
inclination_deg = 55.0
planes = 6
sats_per_plane = 4
phasing_f = 1.0

# 50 W broadband jammer on a 30 m mast, 30 km due east of the ship (ECEF, metres).
[jammer]
position_ecef_m = [2904623.523, 1381438.498, 5489328.347]
power_dbw = 17.0
gain_dbi = 0.0
jammer_type = "broadband"
bandwidth_mhz = 20.0

scenarios.desc: Positioning a low Mars orbiter with a Mars navigation constellation and a deep-space link.
scenarios.kindDesc: Positioning around any solar-system body: an orbiter or a surface lander around a central body chosen by name (Mars, the Moon, Europa, Ganymede, Titan and the rest of the solar-system catalogue), navigating with one-way pseudoranges from a small Walker navigation constellation around the body (two-body orbits with the body's own J2 secular drift, an unknown user clock) and optionally a clock-free deep-space two-way range from the Earth, whose direction and distance come from the analytic solar-system ephemeris at every epoch. Lines of sight are blocked by the body's mean sphere, and a surface user also needs the elevation mask. Per epoch: relays in view, whether the Earth is above the limb, the constellation-only GDOP and PDOP (geometric and position dilution of precision), the formal one-sigma position uncertainty with and without the Earth row, and the error of a seeded Gauss-Newton least-squares fix each way; over the run: availability, Earth visibility, median PDOP, RMS error and median formal sigma, plus the Earth-to-body light time, round trip, Shapiro delay and Sun separation at the epoch. MODELLED: the relay orbits, the noise levels and the instantaneous measurement model are modelling choices, not validated against a mission's navigation data; the body constants are the published values cited in body.rs, and the Earth geometry inherits the solar-system ephemeris labels.
scenarios.toml:
# Positioning a low Mars orbiter with a Mars navigation constellation and a deep-space link.
#
# A 300 km near-polar orbiter navigates around Mars for one sol (88 775 s) from the
# 2027-02-19 opposition, when the Earth is closest and far from a solar conjunction. Two
# kinds of measurement:
#
#   1. ONE-WAY PSEUDORANGES from twelve navigation satellites at 10 000 km in three planes
#      inclined 60 deg (a Walker delta, phasing 1), flown as two-body orbits with the secular
#      drift from Mars' J2 (the second zonal harmonic, its oblateness). The user clock is
#      unknown, so these rows carry a clock column.
#   2. A TWO-WAY RANGE FROM EARTH, clock-free, whenever the Earth is above the Mars limb
#      for the orbiter. The Earth's direction and distance come from the analytic
#      solar-system ephemeris at every epoch.
#
# The report gives, per epoch, the relays in view, the constellation-only dilution of
# precision, the formal position uncertainty with and without the Earth row, and the
# error of a seeded least-squares fix each way; over the sol, the availability and the
# root-mean-square errors, and the Earth-Mars light time and round trip.
#
# MODELLED. The relay orbits, the 1 m range noise and the instantaneous measurement model
# are modelling choices; nothing here is validated against a mission's navigation data.
# The Mars constants are the published values cited in src/body.rs.
kind = "body-pnt"
body = "Mars"
epoch = "2027-02-19T00:00:00"
duration_s = 88775.0
step_s = 300.0
seed = 7

[user]
kind = "orbiter"
altitude_km = 300.0
inclination_deg = 93.0

[constellation]
planes = 3
sats_per_plane = 4
altitude_km = 10000.0
inclination_deg = 60.0
sigma_range_m = 1.0

[earth_link]
enabled = true
sigma_range_m = 1.0

scenarios.desc: Mars PNT — Low-Mars-Orbit user navigated against the simulated MARCONI relay constellation (areostationary relays broadcasting one-way + relaying two-way to a deep-space station) through the joint one-way/two-way radiometric fusion estimator.
scenarios.kindDesc: Deep-space Mars PNT: a simulated MARCONI relay constellation (areostationary + inclined relays broadcasting one-way + relaying two-way to a deep-space station) navigates a reference user (transfer | lmo | surface) through the joint one-way/two-way radiometric fusion estimator. Reports per-epoch geometry/visibility, achieved RMS vs truth, and the formal covariance (1σ / 3σ position) — an honest simulated FoM, NOT a certified protection level.
scenarios.toml:
# Mars PNT — Low-Mars-Orbit user navigated against the simulated MARCONI relay
# constellation (areostationary relays broadcasting one-way + relaying two-way to a
# deep-space station) through the joint one-way/two-way radiometric fusion estimator.
#
# Figures of merit are the estimator's FORMAL COVARIANCE bounds (1σ / 3σ position) and
# the achieved RMS vs a synthetic closed-loop truth — a simulated navigation FoM, NOT an
# aviation-certified protection level (no certified fault model or integrity monitor here).
kind = "mars-pnt"

user = "lmo"                 # ~400 km circular Low-Mars-Orbit, inclined 60°
clock_class = "uso"          # onboard ultra-stable oscillator
step_s = 60.0                # observation cadence
duration_s = 7200.0          # ~one LMO orbit (period ≈ 7100 s)
nmax = 4                     # Mars gravity field degree/order (mars_gmm3, shipped to 4)
range_sigma_m = 1.0          # DSN-class range noise
doppler_sigma_mps = 1.0e-4   # 0.1 mm/s Doppler noise
dynamic_tightness = 0.1      # reduced-dynamic knob (dynamic → kinematic), 0..1
two_way_period_s = 1800.0    # a coherent two-way (clock-free, orbit-pinning) pass every 30 min
seed = 331514052             # deterministic noise seed

scenarios.desc: Mars PNT — a fixed surface user (a lander / rover on the rotating Mars surface) navigated against the simulated MARCONI relay constellation through the joint one-way/two-way radiometric fusion estimator.
scenarios.kindDesc: Deep-space Mars PNT: a simulated MARCONI relay constellation (areostationary + inclined relays broadcasting one-way + relaying two-way to a deep-space station) navigates a reference user (transfer | lmo | surface) through the joint one-way/two-way radiometric fusion estimator. Reports per-epoch geometry/visibility, achieved RMS vs truth, and the formal covariance (1σ / 3σ position) — an honest simulated FoM, NOT a certified protection level.
scenarios.toml:
# Mars PNT — a fixed surface user (a lander / rover on the rotating Mars surface)
# navigated against the simulated MARCONI relay constellation through the joint
# one-way/two-way radiometric fusion estimator.
#
# A surface point is NOT in free-fall — it co-rotates rigidly with Mars (held up by the
# ground), so its dynamics are pure centripetal co-rotation, not orbital free-flight. The
# relays sweeping overhead give the geometric diversity that makes the near-static point
# observable.
#
# Figures of merit are the estimator's FORMAL COVARIANCE bounds (1σ / 3σ position) and
# the achieved RMS vs a synthetic closed-loop truth — a simulated navigation FoM, NOT an
# aviation-certified protection level.
kind = "mars-pnt"

user = "surface"             # fixed point on the equator at the prime meridian (co-rotating)
clock_class = "uso"
step_s = 30.0                # tighter cadence (the relays sweep overhead quickly)
duration_s = 7200.0          # 2 h (several relay passes)
nmax = 4
range_sigma_m = 1.0
doppler_sigma_mps = 1.0e-4
dynamic_tightness = 0.1
two_way_period_s = 1800.0
seed = 331514052

scenarios.desc: Mars PNT — a Mars transfer / capture user (a high, eccentric areocentric arc — the long arc a vehicle flies on approach / in a capture orbit) navigated against the simulated MARCONI relay constellation through the joint one-way/two-way radiometric fusion estimator.
scenarios.kindDesc: Deep-space Mars PNT: a simulated MARCONI relay constellation (areostationary + inclined relays broadcasting one-way + relaying two-way to a deep-space station) navigates a reference user (transfer | lmo | surface) through the joint one-way/two-way radiometric fusion estimator. Reports per-epoch geometry/visibility, achieved RMS vs truth, and the formal covariance (1σ / 3σ position) — an honest simulated FoM, NOT a certified protection level.
scenarios.toml:
# Mars PNT — a Mars transfer / capture user (a high, eccentric areocentric arc — the
# long arc a vehicle flies on approach / in a capture orbit) navigated against the
# simulated MARCONI relay constellation through the joint one-way/two-way radiometric
# fusion estimator.
#
# Figures of merit are the estimator's FORMAL COVARIANCE bounds (1σ / 3σ position) and
# the achieved RMS vs a synthetic closed-loop truth — a simulated navigation FoM, NOT an
# aviation-certified protection level.
kind = "mars-pnt"

user = "transfer"            # high eccentric capture-class arc (perigee ~500 km, apogee ~6 Rm)
clock_class = "dsac"         # a deep-space atomic clock (the most stable class)
step_s = 120.0               # coarser cadence over the long arc
duration_s = 28800.0         # 8 h
nmax = 4
range_sigma_m = 1.0
doppler_sigma_mps = 1.0e-4
dynamic_tightness = 0.1
two_way_period_s = 3600.0    # a two-way pass every hour
seed = 331514052

scenarios.desc: Fused MEO and LEO pseudorange positioning: GPS and Galileo with a LEO navigation layer.
scenarios.kindDesc: Fused medium-Earth-orbit (MEO) and low-Earth-orbit (LEO) positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) over ANY constellations: each [[system]] is a GNSS preset of the constellation-design kind, a LEO preset (xona-pulsar, iridium-stl, starlink-sop, centispace, generic-c-band, the atomic-zero-clock ephemeris model, or another preset file, each in its own file with its sources marked PUBLIC, WORKSHOP or DERIVED), Walker shells or explicit element sets, with a carrier, a chip rate, a carrier-to-noise density (C/N0) envelope from the elevation mask to the zenith, a signal-in-space range error (SISRE), a Doppler sigma and a clock model (its own receiver clock, so the inter-system bias is estimated, or a known broadcast offset). Four modes. DOPPLER: batch Gauss-Newton positioning from range rate with analytic partials, clock-drift and optional velocity states and an optional height constraint, single- or multi-satellite, the error against window length, the Doppler, Doppler-rate and jerk envelope of each LEO system, and the single-pass along-track and cross-track accuracy against the cross-track offset (the cross-track error grows without bound as the pass goes overhead; a single pass also has a mirror solution across the ground track). A Doppler-only signal of opportunity (starlink-sop) runs here. JOINT: per-epoch weighted least-squares pseudorange fixes from GNSS alone, LEO alone and both, per-measurement sigmas from a delay-lock-loop thermal-noise model at C/N0 plus the SISRE (or a fixed sigma, so a signal model can feed them), the estimated inter-system biases, and PDOP/HDOP/VDOP against the number of LEO satellites added. POLAR: satellites in view and DOP against latitude for GNSS, LEO and both. TIMING: time transfer to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) from LEO satellites at a known position with a two-state clock filter whose process noise comes from the engine's oscillator classes, against C/N0 and the oscillator, and the IS-GPS-200 system-time-to-UTC expression; with [timing] trace = true every row also reports its time error and predicted sigma at every epoch. VALIDATED: the largest Doppler of an overhead-to-horizon pass against the published Iridium (up to 36 kHz) and Xona Pulsar X1 (32 to 34 kHz) figures. MODELLED: everything else; the DOP is checked against a hand-derived case, the fixes against their covariance, and the Doppler model against the range-acceleration identity.
scenarios.toml:
# Fused MEO and LEO pseudorange positioning: GPS and Galileo with a LEO navigation layer.
#
# A receiver in Madrid tracks the GPS baseline constellation (GPS SPS Performance Standard,
# 5th edition), Galileo (Walker 24/3/1, Galileo OS SDD) and a LEO navigation constellation
# (the public Xona Pulsar X5 signal: 10.23 Mchip/s in the L5 band, received power -144.9 to
# -136.2 dBW, arXiv:2509.19551). Each system carries its own receiver clock, so the
# inter-system bias of Galileo and of the LEO layer is estimated with the position; the LEO
# pseudoranges are simulated with a 40 ns bias to show it recovered. Every pseudorange's
# sigma is the delay-lock-loop thermal noise at the C/N0 of its elevation combined with the
# system's signal-in-space range error.
#
# The report compares GNSS-only, LEO-only and fused fixes epoch by epoch and gives the PDOP,
# HDOP and VDOP against the number of LEO satellites added to the GNSS geometry (highest
# elevation first). MODELLED.
kind = "leo-pvt"
mode = "joint"
seed = 3
duration_s = 1800.0
step_s = 30.0

[user]
lat_deg = 40.42
lon_deg = -3.70
height_m = 650.0

[joint]
max_leo_sweep = 12

[[system]]
name = "GPS"
preset = "gps-baseline"
cn0_dbhz = [38.0, 48.0]
sisre_m = 0.6

[[system]]
name = "Galileo"
preset = "galileo"
cn0_dbhz = [38.0, 48.0]
sisre_m = 0.3
isb_ns = 12.0

[[system]]
name = "Pulsar X5"
leo_preset = "xona-pulsar"
signal = "X5"
isb_ns = 40.0

scenarios.desc: Lunar navigation SERVICE-VOLUME analysis — Moonlight / LCNS-class constellation.
scenarios.kindDesc: Modelled lunar navigation service-volume analysis from an ILLUSTRATIVE, public-source Moonlight/LCNS-class lunar-orbit constellation (not affiliated with ESA): sweeps a selenographic lat/lon grid over a time horizon and reports DOP / coverage / availability (≥4 sats AND PDOP < threshold) plus a generalised lunar ARAIM protection-level (HPL/VPL) envelope over the volume. The DOP geometry REUSES the gnss_lib_py-VALIDATED kernel (crate::orbit::dop); the protection level REUSES the LunaNet LNIS lunar ARAIM machinery (crate::lunar, σ_URE≈30 m) and reduces to the existing south-pole PL as a special case. MODELLED composition: a circular-/elliptical-Keplerian relay set (not the real differential-corrected LCNS/NRHO ephemeris), a mean-rotation Moon (no libration/precessing pole). Deterministic (pure geometry). No TRL/heritage/agency endorsement.
scenarios.toml:
# Lunar navigation SERVICE-VOLUME analysis — Moonlight / LCNS-class constellation.
#
# Where src/lunar.rs runs a single south-pole protection-level PASS, src/lunar_service.rs
# analyses a whole SERVICE VOLUME: it sweeps a selenographic latitude/longitude grid over a
# time horizon and reports, for an ILLUSTRATIVE Moonlight / LCNS-class lunar-orbit
# constellation:
#
#   * DOP / coverage / availability — the fraction of (grid point, epoch) samples with
#     >= 4 visible satellites AND PDOP < threshold, plus the PDOP and visible-count
#     envelopes. The DOP geometry REUSES the gnss_lib_py-VALIDATED kernel
#     (crate::orbit::dop) exactly — service_dop is a thin filter + that kernel.
#
#   * Generalised lunar ARAIM protection levels (HPL/VPL) over the volume — the SAME
#     LunaNet LNIS lunar ARAIM machinery the south-pole pass uses (crate::lunar::lunar_araim,
#     sigma_URE ~ 30 m, P_sat ~ 1e-4), generalised from the south pole to an arbitrary
#     surface point. At the south pole with the same geometry/budget it reduces to the
#     existing south-pole protection level.
#
# CONSTELLATION (ILLUSTRATIVE; PUBLIC-SOURCE; NOT AFFILIATED WITH ESA): public ESA material
# describes LCNS / Moonlight as a small constellation (~4 satellites, first phase) on
# elliptical lunar frozen orbits favouring south-pole coverage (apolune over the south).
# The defaults below APPROXIMATE that public description (4 sats, eccentric inclined orbit,
# argument of perilune 90 deg so apolune sits over the southern hemisphere). These are
# illustrative parameters for exercising the method, NOT the real Moonlight/LCNS ephemeris,
# and imply no affiliation, endorsement, heritage, certification or TRL.
#
# HONESTY: MODELLED composition. The DOP geometry is validated BY REUSE of the validated
# kernel; the coverage / availability / integrity composition is MODELLED — a circular-/
# elliptical-Keplerian relay set (not a differential-corrected LCNS / 9:2 NRHO ephemeris),
# a mean-rotation Moon (no physical libration / precessing pole), and published LunaNet LNIS
# integrity parameters. This demonstrates the lunar service-volume METHOD, not an
# operational Moonlight availability number. Deterministic (pure geometry; no randomness).
kind = "moonlight-service-volume"

# Illustrative LCNS-class constellation (public-source approximation; not affiliated).
# The public first-phase description is ~4 satellites; the generalised lunar ARAIM
# protection level needs >= 6 satellites IN VIEW (the single-fault hypothesis set needs
# n-1 >= 5 redundancy), so this default uses a fuller (illustrative, expanded) set so the
# PL envelope is exercised alongside the DOP / coverage headline. Set n_sats = 4 to model
# the first-phase constellation (DOP/coverage only; the PL envelope is then empty).
n_sats = 8
sma_km = 9737.4        # ~8000 km perilune altitude above the mean lunar radius
eccentricity = 0.6
inc_deg = 57.7
argp_deg = 90.0        # apolune over the southern hemisphere (south-pole favouring)

# Service-volume grid (south-polar region by default — the Artemis target).
lat_min_deg = -90.0
lat_max_deg = -60.0
lat_step_deg = 10.0
lon_min_deg = -180.0
lon_max_deg = 180.0
lon_step_deg = 60.0

# Time horizon and sampling.
horizon_hours = 12.0
step_min = 60.0

# Geometry / availability thresholds.
elev_mask_deg = 5.0
pdop_threshold = 6.0

# Integrity (LunaNet LNIS): surface-ops alert limit and integrity-risk budget.
alert_limit_m = 50.0
p_hmi = 1e-4

# OPTIONAL per-satellite geometry export for ONE named selenographic site. Off unless
# BOTH coordinates are given; the aggregate coverage / DOP summary above collapses
# per-satellite geometry, but slant range and look angles are what a link budget consumes.
#   export_site_lat_deg = -89.9
#   export_site_lon_deg = 0.0
#
# OPTIONAL transmit antenna for that export. Read only when the export site is also set.
# Each exported row then also carries the off-boresight angle AT THE SATELLITE and the
# transmit gain toward the site from the REAL Airy aperture pattern
# (antenna::pattern_gain_dbi), and the report gains an `antenna_pattern` block reporting
# the in-beam count under that pattern BESIDE the in-beam count under the symmetric
# gain-to-beamwidth approximation (theta_3dB[deg] = sqrt(31000/G_lin)), plus the
# correction between them. Both are emitted; neither replaces the other. The defaults
# below are the engine's own representative lunar transmit aperture, the same 1 m dish at
# 2.4 GHz that scenarios/lunar-attack-surface.toml runs.
#   [export_antenna]
#   diameter_m = 1.0       # required: the pattern is a statement about one aperture
#   carrier_hz = 2.4e9     # default 2.4e9 (S-band lunar AFS)
#   efficiency = 0.60      # default 0.60 (antenna::DEFAULT_APERTURE_EFFICIENCY)
#
# With an export site set, a plain run ALSO emits <scenario>.table.csv: the per-satellite
# geometry in long form, one row per (epoch, satellite), with the row count on the header
# line. This is the largest array the crate publishes — 2304 rows in the released joint
# communications-and-navigation table — and inside JSON it is the shape a naive consumer
# truncates without anything objecting. The four antenna columns are present only when
# export_antenna is configured, and the header says which case the file is. No export
# site, no array, no file.
#
# OPTIONAL real, retrieved geometry in place of the illustrative constellation above.
# UNSET BY DEFAULT, and unset changes nothing: the report is byte-identical to what it is
# without this line. Point it at a file and that file's geometry drives the headline
# coverage / DOP / protection-level figures, the report gains an `ephemeris` provenance
# block (path, SHA-256 of the exact bytes, upstream document, URL, retrieval date), and an
# `ephemeris_comparison` block carries the sigma_URE RANGING REQUIREMENT under that
# geometry BESIDE the unchanged Keplerian and perturbed results, with the difference and
# the ratio emitted as their own named quantities. Nothing is replaced; nothing is tuned to
# bring the geometries together.
#
# Two file formats, two distinct provenance classes (see src/lunar_ephemeris.rs and
# tests/fixtures/lunar_ephemeris/NOTICE.md):
#   * `# format: elements` -> a PUBLISHED CONSTELLATION DEFINITION, propagated by the same
#     Kepler solver the illustrative set uses, so the only difference between the two runs
#     is the constellation design. Provenance class `published-elements`.
#   * `# format: states`   -> a TABULATED MOON-CENTRED STATE EPHEMERIS (what an SPK/BSP
#     kernel evaluates to), Lagrange-interpolated and reduced to MCMF by the IAU 2015 /
#     WGCCRE lunar orientation. Provenance class `published-ephemeris`. A horizon past the
#     end of the table is REFUSED rather than extrapolated.
#
# An `elements` file states its own frame (`# elements_frame: icrf` or `mci`, default
# `mci`) and may give the phase as either a mean or a TRUE anomaly, so a fixture can carry
# exactly the numbers its source printed. An ICRF-stated set is propagated in ICRF and
# reduced by the IAU 2015 / WGCCRE lunar orientation, with no frame approximation; an
# OP-frame set (the Ely / Ely and Lieb convention) is read as MCI, and the report emits the
# COMPUTED tilt that introduces as `ephemeris.published_frame_tie_angle_deg`.
#
# The committed candidates (all regenerable from their recorded sources):
#   ephemeris_path = "tests/fixtures/lunar_ephemeris/lans_demo_ntrs20250009447.csv"
#     the 5-satellite joint ESA/NASA/JAXA LANS interoperability-demonstration reference
#     constellation, Table 3 of Melman et al., ION GNSS+ 2025 / NASA NTRS 20250009447.
#     Elements in ICRF at a stated epoch; the source calls the orbits NOTIONAL and that
#     caveat is emitted with them. Five satellites can never put the six in view ARAIM
#     needs, so this yields coverage and DOP but NO protection level and NO sigma
#     requirement - reported absent, not manufactured.
#   ephemeris_path = "tests/fixtures/lunar_ephemeris/lncss_case_a_navi613.csv"
#     8-satellite LNCSS case study A, Table 1 of Bhamidipati, Mina, Sanchez and Gao,
#     NAVIGATION 70(4) navi.613, 2023 (open access, CC BY). Cases B (12 sats) and C (16)
#     are committed beside it.
#   ephemeris_path = "tests/fixtures/lunar_ephemeris/horizons_lunar_orbiters_2023001_12h.csv"
#     the four spacecraft really in lunar orbit on 2023-01-01, from JPL Horizons. NOT a
#     navigation constellation: 1-2 in view over the south pole, no protection level, so
#     the sigma requirement comes back ABSENT rather than invented.

scenarios.desc: Multi-band jamming waterfall: low Earth orbit (LEO) positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) signals in four bands (UHF, L, S and C) beside GPS and Galileo, each band with its own jammer, drawn as one waterfall per band on one timeline.
scenarios.kindDesc: L-band spectrum model and waterfall: the whole GNSS L band as one power spectral density (PSD), frequency across, time down, over a scripted jammer timeline. SIGNALS: GPS L1 C/A and L2C (BPSK(1)), Galileo E1 open service (MBOC(6,1,1/11), or BOC(1,1)), GPS L5 and Galileo E5a (BPSK(10)), each at its carrier with the interface-specification minimum received power (IS-GPS-200, IS-GPS-705, Galileo OS SIS ICD) unless overridden; GLONASS, BeiDou and Galileo E6 are not modelled. JAMMERS: continuous-wave tone, flat narrowband noise, linear sawtooth chirp and broadband noise matched to a band's own modulation, each with a centre, a bandwidth, a received power (direct, or EIRP and range through the jamming kind's free-space path loss) and on/off times. Each jammer is scored against each band by its spectral separation coefficient kappa over the receiver bandwidth, and (C/N0)_eff = [1/(C/N0) + sum (J/S) kappa]^-1; for one jammer this equals the jamming kind's anti-jam equation with Q = 1/(R_c kappa), and the report carries that cross-check (and the jamming kind's representative-Q figure beside it). The noise floor is k T_sys with T_sys = T_ant + 290 K (F - 1). The waterfall averages each cell over its bin and its row (chirps exactly, whole sweeps plus the partial one; jammers switching mid-row by their duty), so the C/N0 timeline and the picture come from the same numbers; result.json carries the grid block-averaged in power, per-band C/N0 and J/S per row, and per jammer per band the SSC, Q, J/S, in-band J/S and steady C/N0. Optional [iq]: the model drawn as complex IQ at one instant, written to and read back from a SigMF recording (cf32_le or ci16_le), and compared with a Welch estimate. Optional [recording] (native builds): a real SigMF recording's Welch PSD beside the model. VALIDATED: the signal PSDs against the textbook main-lobe widths (BPSK(n) 2n x 1.023 MHz null to null; BOC(1,1) lobes centred at +/-1.023 MHz) and the spectral separation coefficients against their Parseval closed forms and Kaplan & Hegarty's Q = 1 (CW) and 1.5 (matched). MODELLED: jammer powers, timeline, front-end bandwidths, the continuous-spectrum (no code lines) treatment and the absence of AGC, blanking and antenna pattern.
scenarios.toml:
# Multi-band jamming waterfall: low Earth orbit (LEO) positioning, navigation and timing
# (PNT) signals in four bands (UHF, L, S and C) beside GPS and Galileo, each band with
# its own jammer, drawn as one waterfall per band on one timeline.
#
# A LEO-PNT system that spreads its signals over several bands is harder to deny than a
# single L-band system: a jammer built for one band leaves the others alone. This
# scenario shows that with the `spectrum` kind's spectral separation coefficient (SSC)
# chain, band by band. Every signal is public or representative; none depends on a
# particular LEO system:
#   UHF  generic-uhf (465 MHz, BPSK(5) pilot and data, 10 MHz), -150 dBW   [representative]
#   L    xona-x5 (1190.51625 MHz, published), at its -144.9 dBW minimum; GPS L1 C/A and
#        Galileo E5a at their specification minimums
#   S    generic-s (2492.028 MHz, BPSK(5), 16.5 MHz), -150 dBW              [representative]
#   C    generic-c-band-leo (5020 MHz, BPSK(10), 20 MHz), -152 dBW          [representative]
# (BPSK binary phase-shift keying.) The LEO designs are drawn with every component,
# band-limited to their transmit bandwidth.
#
# Timeline (60 s, one row per second):
#   10 s  a continuous-wave (CW) tone at the UHF carrier, -120 dBW received.
#   20 s  a chirp (swept) jammer 16 MHz wide around L1, 9 microsecond sweeps, 50 mW at
#         100 m: it takes GPS L1 C/A and leaves the L5-band signals alone.
#   30 s  wideband (barrage) noise, 40 MHz around 1185 MHz, -118 dBW: it hits Galileo E5a
#         and Xona X5 together.
#   40 s  narrowband noise, 2 MHz at the S carrier, -128 dBW.
#   50 s  noise matched to the C-band signal's own spectrum, -124 dBW.
# The [grid] waterfall is the L band; three [[panels]] add UHF, S and C.
# MODELLED: the signal spectra are validated closed forms; every jammer, power and
# timing here is a scenario input.
kind = "spectrum"
seed = 11
duration_s = 60.0
step_s = 1.0

[receiver]
noise_figure_db = 2.0
antenna_temp_k = 290.0
tracking_threshold_dbhz = 25.0

[grid]
f_min_mhz = 1160.0
f_max_mhz = 1600.0
n_freq = 440

[[panels]]
name = "UHF"
f_min_mhz = 455.0
f_max_mhz = 475.0
n_freq = 200

[[panels]]
name = "S band"
f_min_mhz = 2482.0
f_max_mhz = 2502.0
n_freq = 200

[[panels]]
name = "C band"
f_min_mhz = 5005.0
f_max_mhz = 5035.0
n_freq = 200

[[bands]]
name = "generic-uhf"
signal = "generic-uhf"
signal_power_dbw = -150.0

[[bands]]
name = "gps-l1ca"

[[bands]]
name = "galileo-e5a"

[[bands]]
name = "xona-x5"
signal = "xona-x5"

[[bands]]
name = "generic-s"
signal = "generic-s"
signal_power_dbw = -150.0

[[bands]]
name = "generic-c-band-leo"
signal = "generic-c-band-leo"
signal_power_dbw = -152.0

[[jammers]]
name = "UHF CW tone"
waveform = "cw"
centre_mhz = 465.0
received_power_dbw = -120.0
on_s = 10.0

[[jammers]]
name = "L1 chirp privacy device"
waveform = "chirp"
centre_mhz = 1575.42
bandwidth_mhz = 16.0
sweep_period_us = 9.0
eirp_dbw = -13.0
range_m = 100.0
on_s = 20.0

[[jammers]]
name = "L5-band barrage"
waveform = "wideband"
centre_mhz = 1185.0
bandwidth_mhz = 40.0
received_power_dbw = -118.0
on_s = 30.0

[[jammers]]
name = "S narrowband noise"
waveform = "narrowband"
centre_mhz = 2492.028
bandwidth_mhz = 2.0
received_power_dbw = -128.0
on_s = 40.0

[[jammers]]
name = "C matched noise"
waveform = "matched"
centre_mhz = 5020.0
matched_to = "generic-c-band-leo"
received_power_dbw = -124.0
on_s = 50.0

scenarios.desc: Positioning from a 5G non-terrestrial network (NTN) downlink in the mobile-satellite S band.
scenarios.kindDesc: Positioning from a 5G non-terrestrial network (NTN) downlink in the mobile-satellite service (MSS) S band (3GPP band n256, downlink 2170 to 2200 MHz; default carrier 2172.5 MHz): the Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) on time of arrival, c / (2 pi beta sqrt(2 (C/N0) T)) with beta the root-mean-square (Gabor) bandwidth of the flat OFDM spectrum (B/sqrt(12)), and on the Doppler of a complex tone, sqrt(3 / (2 pi^2 (C/N0) T^3)), for each signal (default a 5 MHz New Radio channel with 4.5 MHz occupied and a 200 kHz narrowband channel with 180 kHz occupied); then, over any LEO constellation, downlink time-of-arrival fixes with an unknown receiver clock (seeded, with the bound plus a network synchronisation error as the sigma), their PDOP and formal 3D sigma, and a single-satellite Doppler fix over the longest pass with the height held. MODELLED: the bandwidth-to-bound step is the textbook closed form, checked against numerical integration of the flat and band-limited BPSK spectra (internal consistency, no published worked figure pinned), and the positioning accuracy is a bound on a multipath-free channel with a stated synchronisation error, not an achieved result.
scenarios.toml:
# Positioning from a 5G non-terrestrial network (NTN) downlink in the mobile-satellite S band.
#
# 3GPP band n256 (downlink 2170 to 2200 MHz, 3GPP TS 38.101-5) serves handsets from
# satellites. A positioning reference signal in a 5 MHz New Radio channel (4.5 MHz occupied)
# or a 200 kHz narrowband channel (180 kHz occupied) bounds the time-of-arrival accuracy
# through its root-mean-square bandwidth: the Cramér-Rao bound is c / (2 pi beta
# sqrt(2 (C/N0) T)), with beta = B / sqrt(12) for a flat spectrum. The scenario compares the
# two channels over a representative NTN shell (324 satellites at 600 km, 55 deg, 10 deg mask), adds a
# 1 m network synchronisation and ephemeris error, and runs downlink time-of-arrival fixes and
# a single-satellite Doppler fix over the longest pass (height held to 10 m).
#
# The bandwidth-to-bound step is a textbook closed form; the positioning accuracy is MODELLED
# (a bound on a multipath-free channel, not an achieved result).
kind = "ntn-positioning"
seed = 5
carrier_hz = 2172.5e6
integration_s = 0.1
doppler_integration_s = 1.0
cn0_dbhz = [38.0, 50.0]
sync_error_m = 1.0
duration_s = 600.0
step_s = 10.0

[user]
lat_deg = 52.5
lon_deg = 13.4
height_m = 40.0

[[signal]]
name = "NR 5 MHz"
bandwidth_hz = 4.5e6

[[signal]]
name = "NB 200 kHz"
bandwidth_hz = 180e3

[[system]]
name = "NTN shell"
role = "leo"
mask_deg = 10.0
[[system.shell]]
total = 324
planes = 18
phasing = 1
altitude_km = 600.0
inclination_deg = 55.0

scenarios.desc: CCSDS OEM interoperability-bridge demonstrator (GMAT / Orekit / STK interop).
scenarios.kindDesc: CCSDS OEM interoperability bridge: import an Orbit Ephemeris Message produced by an external flight-dynamics tool (GMAT/Orekit/STK all emit OEM) and report its segments/objects/frames/epoch-span plus a velocity-consistency check; with no input it round-trips a generated reference orbit and reports the import↔export fidelity. MODELLED structural/physical ingest check, NOT an orbit-accuracy validation of the source.
scenarios.toml:

scenarios.toml:
# GNSS availability derived from orbital geometry (not hand-authored windows).
#
# A spacecraft well inside the GNSS shell (here ~8,000 km altitude) does not have
# continuous coverage: as the constellation moves, the count of satellites that
# clear the elevation mask and are not occulted by Earth rises and falls. The
# visible count is computed from line-of-sight geometry at each step and mapped to
# a GNSS state (>=4 visible = nominal fix, 1-3 = degraded, 0 = denied). When the
# fix drops, the onboard clock must hold time across the gap; the quantum clock
# coasts far longer within a tight timing bound than the chip-scale reference.
# Vendor-neutral; constellation and clock parameters are public/cited.

threshold_ns = 5.0
# Elevation mask (deg) above the user's local horizontal.
mask_deg = 10.0
# 1-sigma user-equivalent range error (m) for the position-accuracy summary;
# position sigma = position-DOP * this. ~1 m is a representative modern
# dual-frequency UERE (Kaplan & Hegarty, Understanding GPS/GNSS).
sigma_uere_m = 1.0

[time]
step_s = 60.0
duration_s = 86400.0   # one day

# User spacecraft at ~8,000 km altitude, inside the GNSS shell.
[user]
altitude_km = 8000.0
inclination_deg = 0.0

altitude_km = 20180.0

sats_per_plane = 4
phasing_f = 1.0

provenance = "Strontium optical lattice clock, space-oriented stability goal sigma_y(1s)=1e-15 (arXiv:1503.08457); lab Sr reaches 4.8e-17 (Oelker et al., Nature Photonics 2019). Not flown."

# GNSS availability for a highly-eccentric (Molniya) user, from orbital geometry.
#
# A Molniya orbit is a 12-hour, highly-eccentric, critically-inclined orbit
# (a ~ 26,600 km, e ~ 0.74, i = 63.4 deg, argument of perigee 270 deg) that
# loiters near apogee over the northern hemisphere. The user spends most of the
# revolution far above the GNSS shell (looking "down" at the constellation, with
# Earth often occulting the far side) and races through perigee below it. The
# visible-satellite count therefore swings widely over the orbit, and during the
# long high-apogee dwell the onboard clock must hold time across the gaps.
#
# The critical inclination (63.4 deg) freezes the argument of perigee under J2;
# `j2 = true` additionally applies the secular nodal regression. Vendor-neutral;
# orbit and clock parameters are public/cited.

kind = "orbit"
seed = 11
threshold_ns = 5.0
mask_deg = 5.0
sigma_uere_m = 1.0

[time]
step_s = 120.0
duration_s = 43200.0   # one ~12 h Molniya revolution

# User on a Molniya orbit. altitude_km sets the semi-major-axis altitude
# (a = 6371 km + 20229 km = 26,600 km); with e = 0.74 the perigee is ~540 km and
# the apogee ~38,900 km. u0_deg = 0 starts the revolution at perigee.
[user]
altitude_km = 20229.0
inclination_deg = 63.4
argp_deg = 270.0
eccentricity = 0.74
u0_deg = 0.0

# GPS-like Walker-delta constellation: 24 satellites, 6 planes, 55 deg inclination,

altitude_km = 20180.0

scenarios.desc: Satellites in view and dilution of precision from the equator to the pole: MEO GNSS alone, a near-polar LEO constellation alone, and both.
scenarios.kindDesc: Fused medium-Earth-orbit (MEO) and low-Earth-orbit (LEO) positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) over ANY constellations: each [[system]] is a GNSS preset of the constellation-design kind, a LEO preset (xona-pulsar, iridium-stl, starlink-sop, centispace, generic-c-band, the atomic-zero-clock ephemeris model, or another preset file, each in its own file with its sources marked PUBLIC, WORKSHOP or DERIVED), Walker shells or explicit element sets, with a carrier, a chip rate, a carrier-to-noise density (C/N0) envelope from the elevation mask to the zenith, a signal-in-space range error (SISRE), a Doppler sigma and a clock model (its own receiver clock, so the inter-system bias is estimated, or a known broadcast offset). Four modes. DOPPLER: batch Gauss-Newton positioning from range rate with analytic partials, clock-drift and optional velocity states and an optional height constraint, single- or multi-satellite, the error against window length, the Doppler, Doppler-rate and jerk envelope of each LEO system, and the single-pass along-track and cross-track accuracy against the cross-track offset (the cross-track error grows without bound as the pass goes overhead; a single pass also has a mirror solution across the ground track). A Doppler-only signal of opportunity (starlink-sop) runs here. JOINT: per-epoch weighted least-squares pseudorange fixes from GNSS alone, LEO alone and both, per-measurement sigmas from a delay-lock-loop thermal-noise model at C/N0 plus the SISRE (or a fixed sigma, so a signal model can feed them), the estimated inter-system biases, and PDOP/HDOP/VDOP against the number of LEO satellites added. POLAR: satellites in view and DOP against latitude for GNSS, LEO and both. TIMING: time transfer to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) from LEO satellites at a known position with a two-state clock filter whose process noise comes from the engine's oscillator classes, against C/N0 and the oscillator, and the IS-GPS-200 system-time-to-UTC expression; with [timing] trace = true every row also reports its time error and predicted sigma at every epoch. VALIDATED: the largest Doppler of an overhead-to-horizon pass against the published Iridium (up to 36 kHz) and Xona Pulsar X1 (32 to 34 kHz) figures. MODELLED: everything else; the DOP is checked against a hand-derived case, the fixes against their covariance, and the Doppler model against the range-acceleration identity.
scenarios.toml:
# Satellites in view and dilution of precision from the equator to the pole: MEO GNSS alone,
# a near-polar LEO constellation alone, and both.
#
# GPS and Galileo orbit at 55 and 56 deg inclination, so north of about 70 deg every MEO
# satellite is on the equatorward half of the sky at low elevation and the vertical geometry
# weakens. The Iridium constellation (six near-polar planes of 11 at 780 km and 86.4 deg, the
# `iridium-stl` preset) converges over the poles. The sweep samples eight longitudes and
# thirteen epochs over two hours at each latitude and reports the mean satellites in view,
# the median PDOP, HDOP and VDOP and the availability (PDOP at or below 6) for each group.
#
# MODELLED: geometry only; ionospheric scintillation, strong at high latitude, is not modelled.
kind = "leo-pvt"
mode = "polar"
duration_s = 7200.0
step_s = 600.0

[polar]
lat_step_deg = 10.0
lon_step_deg = 45.0
pdop_threshold = 6.0

[[system]]
name = "GPS"
preset = "gps-baseline"
mask_deg = 10.0

[[system]]
name = "Galileo"
preset = "galileo"
mask_deg = 10.0

[[system]]
name = "Iridium"
leo_preset = "iridium-stl"
mask_deg = 10.0
